common.ui.SectionHints.21431333e0014a01: The percentage of completed elements of the selected task, rather than the readiness of one neural network request. The counters in the summary show how many photos are ready, waiting, running, or failed. 100% means completion of items, not no errors. The service waiting time does not provide a separate smooth percentage.
common.ui.SectionHints.58120c0fc98408f8: Photos of the selected task and the status of each: waiting, processing, finished result or error. “Hide completed” removes only successfully completed items from this list only; errors remain visible. The task, its results and original photographs are saved.
common.ui.SectionHints.54127eddc7f20e80: Status of the selected run, photo in operation and total counters. After completion, the result of the task remains here. The summary is for a single run; total expenses for the entire history are in the “Expenses” group.
common.ui.SectionHints.a6f8a0fa751cde33: Service, model and parameters with which the selected job is prepared. New job settings do not change this snapshot. The concurrent request limit can be changed for a pending cloud job; Locally, one photo is taken at a time.
common.ui.SectionHints.d7f57f7cbe28c560: Previous launches with date, model, condition and photos. Expand the launch to see its composition. "Open Launch" shows its queue and options above; this button does not restart processing.
common.ui.SectionHints.1fb6427e30b1cdb2: Accounted costs of recognition and editing for the entire saved history. The confirmed cost is separated from the estimate and reserve of requests with an unknown price. These are application statistics, not the service account balance; deleting history changes it.
common.ui.SectionHints.4b6f3204e3c78cad: Photo editing tasks: model, condition, date, duration, dimensions and results. You can open a saved project or a finished frame. Opening a project does not submit a new edit; continuation and cancellation are performed with separate commands.
common.ui.SectionHints.79464c9eae05020a: Index is a list of photos, paths, descriptions and tags saved on the computer. It remains after the program is closed. “Refresh” clarifies information about the database; This button does not start photo recognition. Sources and services are in the groups below.
common.ui.SectionHints.98f00e0046dda393: Folders connected as library sources. The update adds information about new and changed files, preserving the descriptions. Auto-update and exceptions can be configured for each source. Connecting or disconnecting a source does not delete the originals or trigger OCR.
common.ui.SectionHints.72bb3992a997bb5e: Index entries for which the file is unavailable, the path has changed, or requires verification. Select a condition and update the list. Path checking does not run the neural network. Removing from the index removes the stored entry, so check your selections before this separate command.
common.ui.SectionHints.87d294efa58de5db: Copies of the same file with the same content, even if the names or folders are different. This is not a search for similar stories. Before operations with copies, files are checked; viewing and comparing do not delete photos.
common.ui.SectionHints.be1c2e00c59f9799: The copy of the index preserves descriptions, tags, collections, and history, but not the external originals and API keys. The full copy also includes designs, masks and editor images. Recovery replaces the corresponding data after a restart; check the selected copy first.
common.ui.SectionHints.1f19aecab6e67819: The full copy combines the editor's index and storage: projects, history, results and masks. External originals and keys API are not included. Selecting a copy first checks its composition; recovery is applied after restart, preserving the previous storage.
common.ui.SectionHints.b78e1c9601927ad4: Pre-made thumbnails speed up the re-display of photos. Cleaning removes only these previews: the originals, descriptions and tags remain. The next time you view it, the required thumbnails are created again. This shows the cache size and its limitations.
common.ui.SectionHints.59ffdf44e6c4c2f8: Path, version, and service information of the index database for diagnostics and backup. The base path is not the original photos folder. Expanding the group itself does not change anything in the files or index.
common.ui.SectionHints.662a2ff0b698447d: Adding and removing tags from selected photos. Check the preview first, then apply the changes. Descriptions are saved; physical copies of the same photo share its tags. You can change up to 256 different photos in one operation.
common.ui.SectionHints.98427510da0a40bc: Export description and tags to a separate file XMP next to each selected photo. Images are not overwritten and existing XMP images are not replaced. Such files can be transferred along with the photo to programs that support XMP.
common.ui.SectionHints.b715aebc3d1c4d57: Choose where to save the finished images: next to the source, in a specified folder, or with a question each time you save. Projects and cache have separate repositories. The transfer checks the new copy before switching and leaves the old folder.
common.ui.SectionHints.45fe3557333b2f5e: The editor's project storage and preview cache are moved separately. Close the editor before transferring projects. The application will check the copy and keep the previous folder; keys API and general models Ollama are not moved by this action.
common.ui.SectionHints.d803b638dd0c8a83: For a selected saved cloud job: replacing the key and checking the outcome of requests after a communication failure. Checking a known query does not create a new generation. Continuing a task is a separate action; a request without a confirmed outcome requires reconciliation.
common.ui.SectionHints.44f878a96cf7dd92: Requests for which the result or cost has not been confirmed. By ID you can check the status of the service. If the ID is not received, first check the service account: a repetition may lead to additional payment. Manual confirmation only applies to the selected attempt.
common.ui.SectionHints.0890229ca2b43812: Select the recognition service, model level, and the result to save: description, tags, or both fields. Cloud services receive prepared photos and require a separate key. The local model is installed only at your command.
common.ui.SectionHints.2de7174ac7434218: Settings for the following tasks: number of photos, budget, passes and error repetitions. "Concurrent in the cloud" sets the limit of concurrent requests, not the size of the entire queue. One photo is processed locally; an already prepared task stores its own parameters.
common.ui.SectionHints.9f9c56ae102d3b48: The saved description of the selected photo can be edited manually. Changes are saved with a separate button, without accessing the neural network. When updating a result in the background, unsaved text is not automatically replaced.
common.ui.SectionHints.44a0a6929b4c8f97: Events of changes in data and program actions. Select one photo or the entire library, then expand the event for details. The log helps you check what happened; viewing it does not repeat the recorded action.

helpFeatures.choose-folder.title: Choose folder
helpFeatures.choose-folder.explanation: Open the folder with photos on your computer or connected drive. Its contents will appear in Explorer; the source files are not changed. This is selecting a folder to view, not creating an editor project.
helpFeatures.choose-folder.unavailable: Available in the top panel of the main window.

helpFeatures.navigation.title: Navigation
helpFeatures.navigation.explanation: Arrows return to the previous folder, move forward or to a higher level. Breadcrumbs allow you to directly open the parent directory. An inaccessible arrow means that there is no such transition now.

helpFeatures.refresh.title: Update
helpFeatures.refresh.explanation: The main button performs the selected update; the arrow changes the action. The index does not run the neural network.

helpFeatures.workspace-tabs.title: Library Sections
helpFeatures.workspace-tabs.explanation: Switch Explorer, Search, Favorites, Ready Photos, Collections, and Recent Folders. These are different representations of the same library. In the following tour groups, each section is opened separately.

helpFeatures.view.title: View
helpFeatures.view.explanation: Choose a card size, compact list, or file information table. The lower scale controls the same view. When the window is reduced, the button labels are hidden, but their functions remain accessible via icons.

helpFeatures.sort.title: Sort
helpFeatures.sort.explanation: Choose to order by name, dates, or other available information. Separately, you can place folders before files, after them, or together. Changing the order does not move the files themselves on disk.
helpFeatures.sort.unavailable: Available above the grid, except for recent folders.

helpFeatures.table-columns.title: Table Columns
helpFeatures.table-columns.explanation: Plus opens a selection of visible columns; Confirm the set with the “Apply” button. Drag the header border to change the width, double-click to reset. Clicking on a column name changes the sorting.
helpFeatures.table-columns.unavailable: First, select Table view, then open Help again.

helpFeatures.search-scope.title: Where to look
helpFeatures.search-scope.explanation: The current folder with subfolders or the entire indexed library.
helpFeatures.search-scope.unavailable: In Explorer - in the search bar; on the search tab - next to the request.

helpFeatures.search-filters.title: Search filters
helpFeatures.search-filters.explanation: Enter words from descriptions or tags, select a search area and the desired terms. Then click “Search”: changing the fields does not itself replace the current output. If there are no results, try removing some of the restrictions.
helpFeatures.search-filters.unavailable: First, open the “Search” tab and its “Filters”.

helpFeatures.recognition-model.title: Service and model
helpFeatures.recognition-model.explanation: Select local Ollama or cloud Fal AI or OpenRouter, then the model of the selected service. Local work requires an established model; cloud - saved key and consent to send photos. The selection here is used for new assignments.

helpFeatures.recognition-output.title: Output
helpFeatures.recognition-output.explanation: Choose what to save: only quick markup tags, only detailed descriptions, or both results. The setting is applied to the next startup. A field that is not selected for processing retains its original content.

helpFeatures.process.title: Process
helpFeatures.process.explanation: Select the photos and click "Process". By default, they end up in a background job and immediately begin to be recognized. In manual queue mode, you will need to “Start” in the tasks tab. Gray action is not available; If there is no local model, its installation is suggested.
helpFeatures.process.unavailable: Available in the top panel; select photos first.

helpFeatures.settings.title: Settings
helpFeatures.settings.explanation: Separate keys Fal AI and OpenRouter, permission to send photos and parameters of new tasks are saved here. Local models are installed according to your choice. Changing the settings does not change an already created launch.

helpFeatures.queue.title: Tasks
helpFeatures.queue.explanation: This is where recognition tasks work. “Process” creates a run from the selected photos. If the manual queue is enabled, the prepared launch starts working only after “Start”. A pause stops the issuance of new requests, but the already sent one may complete.

helpFeatures.inspector-tabs.title: Right panel
helpFeatures.inspector-tabs.explanation: Details show information about the selected photo; description and tags allow you to edit search markup. Tasks control processing, the library controls the index, and the log shows changes. The width of the panel can be changed using a divider.

helpFeatures.viewer-controls.title: View Control
helpFeatures.viewer-controls.explanation: The arrows move to adjacent photos, the asterisk changes the favorites mark. The edit button opens the current photo in the editor. The slideshow shows the photos in sequence; end it to return to normal browsing.
helpFeatures.viewer-controls.unavailable: Return control by double-clicking on the photo.

helpFeatures.viewer-scale.title: Zoom
helpFeatures.viewer-scale.explanation: “Fit” places the photo in the available area, “1:1” (100%) shows it at a scale of one pixel to one. Magnification helps you see details. These actions only change the view and not the size of the original file.

helpFeatures.viewer-image.title: Photography
helpFeatures.viewer-image.explanation: Double clicking on a photo hides the controls for free viewing; repeated returns it. When zooming in, move the image to view the desired area. Closing the viewer returns to the main program.
helpFeatures.viewer-image.unavailable: Open the photo in the viewer.

helpFeatures.editor-tools.title: Markup
helpFeatures.editor-tools.explanation: Select a point, area, mask, or eraser from the top markup group. A point defines a landmark, an area defines a rectangular area, and a mask defines a shape. Once a point or area is created, selection is enabled and the new group on the right remains collapsed. The brush appears for the mask and eraser. Tag details and additional pictures are on the right; with a narrow window, some of the tools are available through the menu.
helpFeatures.editor-tools.unavailable: Available in the top line of the editor.

helpFeatures.editor-brush.title: Brush size
helpFeatures.editor-brush.explanation: The diameter is set in pixels of the working image: a large brush paints the object faster, a small one helps at the edge. The setting is common for the mask and eraser. The tutorial shows only the controller—the existing markings are not changed.
helpFeatures.editor-brush.unavailable: First select the mask or eraser, close the comparison.

helpFeatures.editor-operations.title: Operations
helpFeatures.editor-operations.explanation: Select an action on the current frame: crop, size, object, background, light, color or other neural network edit. The operation determines the required fields, images, and compatible models. Rotate and flip change orientation along with the markup without a separate history frame.

helpFeatures.editor-instruction.title: Task and place
helpFeatures.editor-instruction.explanation: “Location” selects whose instructions you are currently editing. The run merges all enabled non-empty point and area jobs of the current tool, not just the selected row. General instructions are also taken into account. For an automatic model, text may not be needed; the explanation remains at this place.
helpFeatures.editor-instruction.unavailable: Open "Edit" in the right panel, select an operation with instructions.

helpFeatures.editor-launch.title: Start edit
helpFeatures.editor-launch.explanation: Starts one new edit with all jobs of this tool enabled. Before sending, the composition of the images, model, dimensions, key, consent and budget are checked. Progress is visible on the “Tasks” tab. The result is saved as a separate frame with clean markings; Previous jobs are not automatically resumed.
helpFeatures.editor-launch.unavailable: Expand the right pane and open Edit.

helpFeatures.editor-history.title: Processing history
helpFeatures.editor-history.explanation: Each frame stores its own markup; the new result starts from clean. Pull the border over the ribbon - the cards will grow along with its height, and horizontal scrolling will appear. Ctrl + two frames enables comparison. Drag the frame onto the marker for an additional picture. The trash bin deletes the confirmation frame; subsequent results are saved.
helpFeatures.editor-history.unavailable: Available in the bottom filmstrip of the editor.

helpFeatures.editor-save.title: Save project
helpFeatures.editor-save.explanation: Saves the project with history, selected frame and markup for further work. This is not an export of the final photo. If saving fails, stay in the editor, save again, or choose the provided exit without the latest changes.
helpFeatures.editor-save.unavailable: On a narrow window, available in the editor menu.

helpFeatures.editor-return.title: Return
helpFeatures.editor-return.explanation: Returns to the window from which the editor is open, and closes the editor after deciding whether to save. If there are unsaved changes, choose to save, continue, or exit without them. The original photo remains on the disk.
helpFeatures.editor-return.unavailable: Available on the left in the single top row.

helpFeatures.appearance.title: Subject
helpFeatures.appearance.explanation: Switches between light and dark appearance; the photos remain the same.
helpFeatures.appearance.unavailable: The moon or sun button is located on the right in the top panel of the main window.

helpFeatures.search-saved.title: Saved Searches
helpFeatures.search-saved.explanation: Words, search area and filters are saved, not photos. Select the saved terms and click “Search” to get the current results. An empty list means that the conditions have not yet been saved.
helpFeatures.search-saved.unavailable: Available in the “Saved” tab of the search.

helpFeatures.search-actions.title: Actions with results
helpFeatures.search-actions.explanation: The output menu copies paths, opens folders and exports CSV/JSON. Exports details of the results rather than copies of the photos. Select a photo to act on the selection; Without a search applied, the menu is not available.
helpFeatures.search-actions.unavailable: Located to the right of the search tabs.

helpFeatures.favorites-workspace.title: Favorites
helpFeatures.favorites-workspace.explanation: The star adds the photo to your favorites. Here are tagged photos from the indexed library, regardless of folder. Pressing the star again clears the checkmark, but does not delete the file. If the list is empty, mark any photo in the explorer.

helpFeatures.processed-workspace.title: Finished photos
helpFeatures.processed-workspace.explanation: Photos with saved processing results are collected here. You can search, open, and change their descriptions and tags. Indexing a file by itself does not make it ready. In the empty section, first edit the photo or save its description.
helpFeatures.processed-workspace.unavailable: The “Completed” section is above the grid.

helpFeatures.collections-workspace.title: Collections
helpFeatures.collections-workspace.explanation: A collection is a named collection of links to photographs. Create a selection, then add selected photos; the files themselves remain in their folders. Open a collection to see its contents. Deleting a collection does not delete the originals.

helpFeatures.recent-workspace.title: Recent folders
helpFeatures.recent-workspace.explanation: Here are the paths of recently opened folders. Click the path to return. If the drive is disconnected or the folder is renamed, connect the drive or open a new path; photos are not stored inside the recent list.
helpFeatures.recent-workspace.unavailable: The "Recent folders" section is above the grid.

helpFeatures.description-panel.title: Description of the photo
helpFeatures.description-panel.explanation: Select a photo and edit the search text. Formatting changes the appearance, and Save Description writes the text into the index. “Reset” returns the saved option. Changing the text does not redraw the photo.
helpFeatures.description-panel.unavailable: Select a photo: a description field will appear on the right.

helpFeatures.tags-panel.title: Photo tags
helpFeatures.tags-panel.explanation: Short words and expressions help you find photos. Separate them with commas, semicolons, or lines, then save. Batch tags in the drop-down group add or remove common tags from multiple selected photos.
helpFeatures.tags-panel.unavailable: Select a photo to edit its tags.

helpFeatures.journal-panel.title: Changelog
helpFeatures.journal-panel.explanation: Actions with photos and metadata are recorded here. Expand the entry to compare the old and new values. An empty log means there are no recorded actions in this library; it is not a history of cloud payments.

helpFeatures.queue-progress.title: Overall progress
helpFeatures.queue-progress.explanation: Shows the percentage of completed items for the selected run. For three photos, completion of the first gives 33%, the second - 67%, the third - 100%. Erroneous, canceled and missed elements are also completed: 100% does not mean that all photos are recognized successfully.

helpFeatures.queue-items.title: Queue elements
helpFeatures.queue-items.explanation: Shown here are photos of the selected run and the condition of each. The "Hide completed" in the header hides only successfully completed rows, without deleting files or results. Errors remain visible. The list scrolls within the available panel space.

helpFeatures.queue-details.title: Launch Summary
helpFeatures.queue-details.explanation: Expand to see the number of pending, completed, failed, canceled photos and the current request. Completion or stop is also shown here. This information applies to the selected run, not the entire library.

helpFeatures.queue-settings.title: Job Options
helpFeatures.queue-settings.explanation: These are the saved parameters of the selected run: service, model, passes and restrictions. Changing settings for new tasks does not change old ones. In an unfinished cloud run, you can separately change the concurrent request limit; passes of one photo are performed sequentially.

helpFeatures.queue-history.title: Launch history
helpFeatures.queue-history.explanation: One run combines photos added together. Open it to see the photos and their results in the item list. Viewing a completed run does not reprocess the photo. Old launches are loaded when scrolling through history.

helpFeatures.index-library.title: Library and index
helpFeatures.index-library.explanation: The index stores paths, descriptions, tags, and information about photos on this computer. It is saved after the program is closed. “Refresh” here rereads the database information; This is not re-recognizing photos or scrubbing descriptions.
helpFeatures.index-library.unavailable: Open "Library" in the right pane of the main window.

helpFeatures.library-roots.title: Connected folders
helpFeatures.library-roots.explanation: The connected folder is the source of the library. Its update adds file information and tracks changes without editing the originals or calling the model. Configure exceptions and auto-update separately for each source. Disabling the source preserves the index and descriptions.

helpFeatures.index-maintenance.title: Problem entries
helpFeatures.index-maintenance.explanation: Path checking detects inaccessible, moved, or erroneous files. First, repair the disk or check the path; Removing an entry from the index is a separate action. The scan does not run recognition and does not automatically delete sources.

helpFeatures.index-duplicates.title: Exact duplicates
helpFeatures.index-duplicates.explanation: Groups of matching files allow you to check copies of one photo. Check the paths before making a decision: the same name does not mean the same content. This section is not just looking for similar stories.

helpFeatures.index-backup.title: Index backup
helpFeatures.index-backup.explanation: The copy preserves local information and descriptions. Please transfer original photos separately. Before restoring, check the date and composition of the copy: restoring changes the current index. Tour does not perform the recovery for you.

helpFeatures.index-cache.title: Thumbnail cache
helpFeatures.index-cache.explanation: The cache speeds up the display of photos. Cleaning removes only the prepared thumbnails; they are created again the next time you view them. Sources, descriptions and tags are preserved. If a particular preview fails, try uploading that photo again first.

helpFeatures.index-technical.title: Technical details
helpFeatures.index-technical.explanation: The database version and path are needed for diagnostics and backup. This is the index location, not the folder of all photos. The path can be copied; For normal viewing, this section can be left closed.

helpFeatures.editor-canvas.title: Web and movement
helpFeatures.editor-canvas.explanation: The selected frame and its markings are visible on the canvas. The wheel changes scale; hand or middle button moves the image. A dot indicates a location, a rectangular area defines an area, and a mask paints the exact shape. Escape cancels an incomplete gesture.
helpFeatures.editor-canvas.unavailable: Open the photo in the editor.

helpFeatures.editor-models.title: Model selection
helpFeatures.editor-models.explanation: The “Economy”, “Balanced” and “Quality” levels help you choose a model; Below is a list of compatible options. The question mark after “Model” explains limitations and observations about placement accuracy. Price is an estimate of the entire launch. Entry limit includes source. Resolution and available quality are set separately under the model.

helpFeatures.editor-export.title: Save image
helpFeatures.editor-export.explanation: Exports the selected frame to a file taking into account the working orientation. For an intermediate result, select the desired frame in the history. Saving the project separately saves the markup and history: one project is not enough to get the final JPG/PNG.
helpFeatures.editor-export.unavailable: On the top line of the editor.

helpFeatures.smart-rename.title: Smart renaming
helpFeatures.smart-rename.explanation: Opens a window of future names for the selected files or folder; without selection, the current folder is used. Specify the common name, prefix, suffix, and numbering. Check the order in the preview before applying. Photos are not redrawn, the neural network is not called. Cancellation is available in the rename log.
helpFeatures.smart-rename.unavailable: Open the folder or select the files you need. The tag icon is located in the top bar.

helpFeatures.editor-markup.title: Tags and additional pictures
helpFeatures.editor-markup.explanation: cards of points and regions are first collapsed. Plus, next to the photo counter, selects a file and expands the desired group. A frame from the bottom filmstrip can be dragged directly onto the label: the only additional image at the point is replaced, and a new one is added at the area. The eye changes visibility, the checkbox changes participation in the request. The handle below changes the height of the list.
helpFeatures.editor-markup.unavailable: Open the "Edit" tab. No new labels are created during tour.

helpFeatures.editor-model-filters.title: Model filters
helpFeatures.editor-model-filters.explanation: The funnel icon opens conditions instead of levels: price of the entire launch, resolution, number of additional images without source, and support for original size. The conditions select the list, but do not send a request or automatically select another model. The cross returns the normal selection.
helpFeatures.editor-model-filters.unavailable: Open Edit and close the crop or resize window.

helpFeatures.editor-output.title: Resolution and quality
helpFeatures.editor-output.explanation: Resolution specifies the dimensions in pixels; quality - available mode of the model. These are different settings. “Like source” requires support for the original dimensions. If you select 1K/2K or another mode, a new size is requested. Some tools specify a scale instead of a resolution; unnecessary fields are not shown.
helpFeatures.editor-output.unavailable: Fields vary by model. To expand the image, set the margins on the sides; to enlarge, set the available scale. If filters are open, close them first.

helpFeatures.editor-tasks.title: Editing tasks
helpFeatures.editor-tasks.explanation: Open the title of the desired card: its dates, duration, model, dimensions and results are revealed inside. “Open” selects a finished frame without a new generation. Estimation and confirmed consumption are separated. The list uses all available height; old tasks do not continue automatically.
helpFeatures.editor-tasks.unavailable: Go to the Tasks tab on the right. Before the first edit, the empty state is shown here.

helpFeatures.editor-sources.title: Project sources
helpFeatures.editor-sources.explanation: Images added to the project are stored here. Selecting an image opens its working image; This is not an attachment to a tag. To use a frame as an additional picture, drag it from the bottom filmstrip to a point or area in the markup. Import and deletion are performed only at your command.
helpFeatures.editor-sources.unavailable: Open the "Sources" tab in the right pane of the editor.

models.editor.help.banana-b: Edits photos according to description and uses additional pictures. It's a more cost-effective option than the Nano Banana Pro for most common edits. After processing, compare important inscriptions and faces with the original. Resolution, web search and number of results affect the price.
models.editor.help.banana-pro-q: Complex instructions, compositions and work with several additional pictures. More expensive than regular Nano Banana. For important text and faces, compare the result with the source. Resolution upgrades and web searches cost extra.
models.editor.help.object-e: Quickly remove an object inside a mask. Use the brush to select everything that needs to be removed, including the shadow. Text instructions are not sent. Economy mode may be less able to restore complex backgrounds.
models.editor.help.object-b: Removing an object using a mask with more thorough restoration of the background. Instructions are not used; the action is determined by the mask. For large objects and repeating patterns, the result should be compared with the original.
models.editor.help.object-q: Removes an object by mask in the best quality mode of the Object Removal family. Paint over the entire object, including any unnecessary shadow; text instructions are not sent. Even this mode cannot reliably restore details hidden by the object being removed.
models.editor.help.eraser-b: Removing an object from the white area of the mask and filling it with the surrounding background. Works with one source, without additional pictures and text instructions. For careful removal, grab the edges of the object and its shadow.
models.editor.help.fill-q: Fills the mask area according to instructions: for example, you can describe the background that should appear instead of a removed object. Does not accept additional pictures. The price depends on the number of pixels in the result.
models.editor.help.pixelcut-b: Automatically separates the main subject and removes the background. The original image is enough: a mask, text and additional images are not needed. After treatment, check hair, fur, thin edges and translucent areas.
models.editor.help.ideogram-bg-b: Automatically removes background from one image; the main object selects the service. Text and additional images are not used. The model is designed to produce transparent results; Check the background and edges of the object before saving.
models.editor.help.bria-bg-q: Separates the object and makes the background transparent. The mask and additional pictures are not used. If desired, specify in text which object to leave: for example, only the chair. The text instructions change the rate, so check the estimate before you start.
models.editor.help.outpaint-e: Quickly continues the scene beyond the edges of the photograph. Set the size of the new fields in pixels. Text and additional images are not used. If the response matches the requested canvas, the program saves the original pixels; for other sizes, shows the model's response with a warning.
models.editor.help.outpaint-q: A more thorough mode of continuing the scene beyond the edges. Accepts one source and the sizes of new fields, without text instructions and additional pictures. The price depends on the size of the source and the result. Accurate preservation of the original pixels is possible if the size of the response matches the requested canvas; otherwise the response is shown with a warning.
models.editor.help.expand-b: Expands the canvas according to the specified dimensions and position of the source. If desired, add instructions in English. The original photograph must occupy at least 15% of the area of ​​the new canvas. Additional pictures are not used.
models.editor.help.ideo-replace-e: Changes the background in fast TURBO mode. Describe a new scene, such as a sunny garden. The service itself determines the main object. The request includes only the original photo; additional images remain in the project, but are not sent. Check the complex edges of the object on the result.
models.editor.help.ideo-replace-b: Changes the background in BALANCED mode, which combines speed and quality. Describe the environment that should appear behind the object. Only the original photo is included in the request. After processing, check whether the desired object and its shadows are preserved.
models.editor.help.ideo-replace-q: Changes the background in QUALITY mode - the most expensive in this family. Describe your desired environment. The service itself determines the main object; The request includes only the original photo, without additional images. Compare the result with the original, especially the edges of the main object.
models.editor.help.crisp-e: Inexpensively enlarges a photo and enhances clarity. Text, markup and additional images are not sent. Suitable for fast processing; severe smearing and poorly distinguishable small letters may not be corrected.
models.editor.help.seedvr-e: Enlarges one image by a factor or to the selected resolution. Text and additional images are not used. The price depends on the number of megapixels of the source and the result; the model can fill in small details.
models.editor.help.clarity-b: Enlargement with controlled drawing of details. The instructions can clarify the content of the scene; similarity and creative freedom are specified separately. With high freedom, faces and inscriptions can change.
models.editor.help.precision-b: Enlarges the image using the Topaz Standard V2 algorithm, trying to preserve the structure of the source. Works with one photo; Facial restoration is enabled separately. The size of the finished image affects the cost, so check the estimate before you go.
models.editor.help.precision-q: Enlargement of Topaz High Fidelity V3 with an emphasis on preserving the original parts. Does not accept additional pictures or text instructions. For documents and faces, be sure to compare the finer details of the result.
models.editor.help.dust-q: Topaz Dust-Scratch V2 removes dust and scratches from a single image. Markup and text do not control processing. Preservation of the original color is configured separately. Compare the result with the original to check whether the useful texture has disappeared along with the defects.
models.editor.help.flash-e: Performs inexpensive edits based on descriptions with several additional pictures. The service can downsample input images to one million pixels, so check the output for small lettering and faces. The allowed number of images and the size of the result are specified in the model parameters.
models.editor.help.klein-e: Fast version for simple changes and a small number of additional images. Complex faces, inscriptions and small details need to be compared with the original.
models.editor.help.grok-e: Edits a photo according to a text task and accepts up to two additional images. In automatic mode, the aspect ratio is selected based on the first image. Describe how to use each attached picture.
models.editor.help.seed-lite-b: Edits photographs and composes compositions with several additional pictures. The result size is more than one million pixels; For a very small copy after generation, normal resizing can be used.
models.editor.help.flare-b: Editing according to detailed instructions with several additional pictures. The initial quality mode is medium; it can be changed in the available options. The cost depends on the volume of text and images.
models.editor.help.sunburst-q: Edits a photograph according to detailed instructions; The default is High quality. The price depends on the size, text and number of images. If local editing is needed, check the support of the selected markup. Compare important details with the source before saving.
models.editor.help.seed-pro-q: Edits photographs and composes compositions with several additional pictures. The image limit shown includes the source. The size of the result and the number of investments affect the estimate of the launch cost.
models.editor.help.rembg-e: Automatic background removal without text instructions. Check thin edges and translucent objects.
models.editor.help.birefnet-q: Removing the background while maintaining thin edges and transparency. Payment depends on calculation time; The amount before launch is approximate. Check hair, fur and translucent areas.
models.editor.help.wonder-q: Enlargement with additional drawing Wonder 3.5. Faces, inscriptions and small details must be compared with the original.
models.editor.help.creative-q: Enlarges the image while adding new details. Suitable for creative enhancement, but may change letters, facial features and texture. If the accuracy of the document or original features is important, compare the result with the original.
models.editor.help.iclight-q: Changes the lighting of the photo. Use a mask to designate the object for which you want to adjust the light, and describe the desired lighting in the instructions. In this operation, the mask represents the object to be illuminated, rather than the area to be removed.
models.editor.help.nafnet-e: Reduces photo blur. This mode is designed for lubrication; To correct scratches, color and other damage to an old photo, choose a suitable restoration model.
models.editor.help.photo-restore-b: Corrects scratches on an old photo. For this model, the program accepts pictures with aspect ratios of 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, 4:3 or 3:4. If the source is of a different shape, it is not cropped automatically: first prepare a suitable frame or select a different model.

helpArticles.folders.title: Getting started and folders
paragraphs: “Choose folder” opens a folder of photos. It does not open an editor project. Use Back, Forward, Up and the breadcrumbs to change the current folder. “Subfolders” controls whether files in nested folders are included.

“Recent folders” keeps links to folders you have opened before. If a folder is unavailable, check that its drive is connected; its photos have not been deleted. Manage connected folders on the “Library” tab in the right panel.

helpArticles.refresh.title: Refreshing folders and the index
paragraphs: The menu beside Refresh selects what the main button does. “Refresh folder” reads the folder contents again; “Refresh folder index” updates the locally stored information. The button’s icon and tooltip reflect your choice. Neither action starts AI processing.

The index is a local catalog of files, metadata, descriptions and tags used for searching. “Refresh order” sorts the displayed items again using the selected criterion. Background recognition does not rearrange cards that are already displayed.

helpArticles.library.title: Browsing the library
paragraphs: Explorer shows the current folder. Favorites contains starred photos; Completed contains photos with processing results; Collections contains your own groups; Recent folders keeps links to folder paths. Being in the index does not by itself mean that a photo has a description.

“View” and the scale control at the bottom offer four card sizes, a list and a table. Folders always appear before files; the selected sort order applies within each group. Search results follow the search ordering.

In the table, click a column heading to sort, or drag a column boundary to change its width. You can also use the arrow keys on a focused boundary (Shift gives a larger step). Escape cancels the current adjustment; a double-click restores the default width. The plus button on the right lets you choose visible columns. Confirm with “Apply”.

helpArticles.search.title: Searching and selecting
paragraphs: Choose where to search: the current or selected folder and its subfolders, or the entire indexed library. Enter words, choose filters and click “Search”. Expand the additional filters when you need them. Existing results stay visible until you run the new search.

Search uses descriptions, tags and the matching method you choose. Photos without descriptions are harder to find by their content. Ctrl toggles individual selections; Shift selects a range. Selecting all results also includes pages that have not loaded yet.

The “Saved” tab stores search conditions, not copies of files. Choose a saved search, then run it. More results load as you scroll. Result actions let you copy paths, open folders and export CSV/JSON files containing metadata and links. They do not move the originals. Export uses the applied search and selection.

helpArticles.recognition.title: Image recognition
paragraphs: Recognition creates text and tags for search and is different from image editing. Select the service, available model and result: description, tags or both. Local models require an installed service and a downloaded model; cloud ones need a key.

Fast modes reduce time but may miss details. A detailed description lists the main objects, background, surroundings and minor details. Repeated passes check the result, increasing time and possible costs; the coincidence of answers does not guarantee truth.

Click "Process" for the selected photos. By default, jobs start immediately; setting up a manual queue leaves them waiting to be explicitly run. The photo limit per launch and the number of simultaneous requests are different settings.

If the selected local model is not installed, the button says “Install model”. The service and model are downloaded only when you choose to install them; existing components are reused. A disabled “Process” button means no suitable photos are selected or preparation is still in progress.

helpArticles.privacy.title: Keys, consent and costs
paragraphs: Fal AI and OpenRouter keys are stored separately in each service’s settings. Saving a key and checking access are separate actions. Windows protects the key for the current user. Do not put it in a photo description or an activity log.

Cloud processing sends the selected images and instructions to a third-party service. If suitable permission has not been saved, a consent dialog appears. Declining prevents the request from being sent. Local recognition does not require this consent.

The price before a run is an estimate based on the current catalog and parameters. It does not confirm a charge. Masks, variants, resolution and model affect the cost. Check actual charges with the service. If a submission’s outcome is unknown, check it before trying again to avoid paying twice.

helpArticles.queue.title: Recognition tasks
paragraphs: In the main window, the Tasks tab refers to recognizing descriptions and tags. “Queue Items” shows photos of the selected run, “Run Summary” shows its status and counters, “Job Parameters” shows saved settings. Groups are expanded independently. History allows you to open a previous run without reprocessing. Photo editing tasks are located separately - in the editor and in the “Photo Editing” group.
Pausing stops new jobs from being issued, but the submitted request may complete. Continue resumes the queue. Stopping does not guarantee cancellation and refund on the service side.

The number of simultaneously processed photos is set separately from the number of passes of one photo. In a cloud work-in-progress, the concurrency limit can be changed; One photo at a time is processed locally. “Hide completed” in the list header hides only successfully completed rows, leaving errors. Results and history are saved.

helpArticles.inspector.title: The right panel
paragraphs: “Details” shows the selected photo and its information. “Description” and “Tags” let you edit the text results. Reset discards unsaved changes in the field; Save stores the result in the index. Editing descriptions or tags does not change the image.

Batch tags let you add or remove tags across several selected photos. Expand the group when you need it. XMP export writes separate files beside the photos; existing files are protected against accidental replacement.

“Library” contains connected folders, write problems, exact duplicates and backups. An index backup keeps local information without external originals or API keys; a full backup also includes editor storage. Backup contents are checked before a restore is prepared. The restore takes effect after a restart. In “Activity log”, expand an entry to read what changed without repeating the action.

helpArticles.viewer.title: Viewing photos
paragraphs: Photos fit the available space without cropping. Use the side arrows to browse and the mouse wheel to zoom. “1:1” shows one image pixel per viewing pixel; “Fit” brings the entire image back into view. Rotation changes only the view. In a narrow window, some button labels are hidden; their names remain available in tooltips.
Double-click to hide or restore the controls. The slideshow uses a full-screen view with unobtrusive buttons. “Edit” opens the built-in editor; “Edit image” opens an external application.

The menu offers saving a copy, resizing and showing the file in Explorer. Delete moves the file to the Recycle Bin after confirmation. Printing, sharing, external editing and setting the desktop background depend on Windows and installed applications. Availability of a command does not guarantee that the external action will finish.

“Resize image…” is in the three-dot menu. Choose dimensions, whether to keep the aspect ratio and the output format. JPEG quality is set separately. Saving creates a new file. For TIFF files, the app may display a smaller preview of the first page; the original dimensions are shown separately and differ from the preview resolution.

helpArticles.editor.title: Editor: Annotations and tools
paragraphs: The panel on the left selects the action on the current image. Cropping and resizing are done without a neural network; the remaining tools use the selected compatible model. Available settings vary by tool.
The top icons are divided by purpose: select and move, point and area, mask and eraser, undo and redo, reflections. Scale and Fit are on the right. The name of each icon appears on hover.

A point marks a location, an area defines a rectangle and a mask defines a painted shape. Object removal usually needs a mask; a model with text support can also use instructions. The brush diameter is measured in working-image pixels. Escape cancels an unfinished gesture.

On the right are annotations, instructions and model selection. Selecting “Location” changes the instruction being edited, and when running, all enabled annotations with a non-empty assignment of this tool are taken into account. The eye controls visibility, the checkbox controls participation in the request. For more information about additional pictures and tasks, see the article “Editor: tasks and additional pictures.”

Rotations and reflections change the working orientation along with the markings, without creating a frame in the filmstrip. Cropping and resizing create a separate image after you apply them. The result of the model must be compared with the source: cost and quality level do not guarantee accuracy.

helpArticles.results.title: History and saving
paragraphs: The bottom filmstrip contains the source and independent images of the result. Click an image to open its image and saved markup. The new result starts with clean markup; returning to the previous image restores its marks and assignments.

Pull the top border of the filmstrip: Thumbnails expand in both height and width, so fewer images fit at once. The filmstrip scrolls horizontally. The height is common for all images and does not change when selecting another.

For comparison, hold Ctrl and select two images, then move the divider on the image. The comparison does not apply the changes. For an additional picture, drag the image to the desired mark on the right.

The trash can in the thumbnail removes this particular image from the filmstrip after confirmation. Shift + click selects multiple images; Shift + Trash deletes the selected ones. The source is protected. Deleting the previous image does not delete its subsequent results: they are independent. Hidden images is available in the change history.

"Project" saves history and markup for continuation; “Image” saves the selected image to a separate file. Enable autosave from the menu. If it is turned off, you can save changes, stay, or exit without the latest edits before exiting. If a save error occurs, the editor stays open rather than falsely reporting a successful save.

“Back” returns you to the window from which the editor is open. “Start over” creates a separate clean project from the source; the previous project and its results are preserved. Keys and cloud jobs are not resent when viewing history.

helpArticles.appearance.title: Help, topics and problems
paragraphs: The moon or sun button on the right side of the top panel of the main window switches the light and dark theme of open windows. Photos, markings and task parameters do not change. The photo view keeps the image's dark surroundings, and its dialogs follows the selected theme.

“Show me around” navigates through function groups and opens the necessary tabs. The "Reference" contains searchable articles. Buttons with a question mark next to the headings provide short help: hover the mouse, click to pin, or navigate to the button using the Tab key. Escape closes the tooltip. Tour does not trigger processing, deletion, or payment.

If there is a thumbnail error, retrying that thumbnail is available; the original file is not overwritten. If the photo opens but there is no preview, check the error message and thumbnail cache. Logs are useful for diagnostics, but keys should not be included in them. An unknown cloud request status is first checked rather than resubmitted.

helpArticles.editor-instruction-guide.title: Editor: tasks and additional pictures
paragraphs: First select the tool on the left. To change the background, describe the desired background in the main field: for example, “Light studio, soft daylight, leave the person unchanged.” Jobs from another tool are not added to this request.

To edit locally, place a dot or select an area. In the “Location” field, select the desired annotation and write what to add or change. Switching the location allows you to edit its text; it does not turn off other tasks. A single run combines the instructions of all included non-empty annotations and the general instruction, if one is specified.

Each annotation has its own instructions and additional pictures. The eye only hides it on the canvas; the checkbox determines whether it is included in the request. Instructions for a hidden but enabled annotation still participate. Check every included annotation before starting.

A point has one additional image with replacement, while areas have several. Click the plus next to the photo counter to select a file: the collapsed group will open itself. You can also take an image from the bottom filmstrip and drag it directly to the desired point or area in the markup list. At a point, dragging replaces an additional image, at an area it adds. Working rotations and reflections of the image are taken into account.

In an open group, you can view, rearrange, temporarily exclude, or unpin additional pictures. The order of additional pictures and their association with the annotation are transmitted along with the task. The general limit near the model includes the source; the same image used in multiple places does not necessarily take up multiple inputs. Detaching an additional image does not delete the original file.

To remove an object, paint over the desired area with a mask; The eraser corrects its edges. If the selected model does not accept text or additional pictures, this data is not sent. They remain in the project for the compatible tool. The model tooltip and “What will be sent” preview show applicable inputs.

The handle under the markup changes the height of the list; double click returns the height to the content. When manually stretching, the following fields are moved down and the long list is scrolled. All saved additional pictures can be found in additional settings; their number may differ from the number of inputs of the current edit.

Select your model, resolution, and available quality, check the cost estimate, and click “Start edit”. All jobs for this run are submitted together. The finished image is selected automatically if you have not moved on to another project; the new image has clean markings, while the original one retains the previous marks and tasks.

helpArticles.editor-safe-workflow.title: Editor: from source to result
paragraphs: Selecting an image in the bottom filmstrip makes it the starting image for the next edit. Each image keeps its own annotations and instructions. You can remove it independently of later results. The filmstrip height applies to all images.

Select a tool, specify instructions or a mask, and attach additional pictures if needed. All enabled non-empty jobs of the current tool participate in local editing. Different places and additional images are combined into one request. The accuracy of the location depends on the selected model and scene.

The “Economy”, “Balanced” and “Quality” levels help you choose a model option; the drop-down list contains the available options for this tool. The question mark after “Model” explains the purpose, limitations, number of additional pictures and observations about the accuracy of placement.

The filter icon in the model heading shows filters instead of tiers. Filter by estimated cost for the full run, resolution, number of additional pictures excluding the original, or support for original dimensions. Filters narrow the list; you still choose the model separately. The cross resets them. If no model matches, relax the filters.

Resolution and quality of the result are different settings under the list of models. The size specifies the number of pixels, the quality specifies the mode of the selected model, if available. “Like source” requires support for original dimensions; If incompatible, please select another size or model. Explicitly selecting 1K, 2K, or another available mode sets the new size. The final dimensions are also shown in the task.

The cost estimate applies to the entire current run and changes with the parameters and composition of the inputs. It is not a confirmed charge. Additional settings include budget, parallelism and detailed query composition. Without the required cloud send permission, a consent window will appear.

Clicking “Start edit” creates a new task. Old interrupted or unknown submissions do not themselves continue and do not block a separate new edit. Monitor progress on the “Tasks” tab; simply opening the card does not resend photos.

While an edit is running, changes to its original instructions and another run of this project are blocked. You can still view and move the canvas, cancel or close the window. The result appears as a separate image. Saving the project and saving an image use different buttons.

helpArticles.rename.title: Smart renaming
paragraphs: Select the files or folder you want and click the Smart Rename tag icon in the top bar. Without selection, the current folder is used. A separate window will open with proposed names. The neural network and paid requests are not used.

You can keep the same name or set a general one, add a prefix and suffix. For example, the general name “Product” and numbering with three digits will give “Product_001”, “Product_002” and so on. The extension is added automatically and does not change.

The "Numbering" switch turns the number on or off. Specify the beginning, number of digits and position of the number. "Order" determines which file will receive the first number; Before confirming, check the sequence using the thumbnails and names in the preview.

You can include subfolders for a folder; The names of the folders themselves do not change. Additional parameters include the counter step and, for multiple folders, a separate counter start in each folder. Use only the conditions you need and check the final list.

Rename applies the shown plan only after checking for conflicts and file changes. Photo content and metadata are preserved and library paths are updated. If the name is taken or the file has changed, correct the conditions and update the preview.

On the “Log and undo” tab, you can check the result, continue the interrupted operation, or cancel it. Continuation occurs only at your command; If there is a conflict with a modified file, the application does not overwrite it. For another set, close the window and select the files again.

helpArticles.editor-tasks.title: Editor: tasks and results
paragraphs: The Tasks tab on the right side of the editor shows the tasks of the current project. Click the title of the desired card: details will open inside it, next to its results. The list scrolls to the full available height of the panel.

The card indicates the date of creation and completion, time before the result and after the start of execution, model, original, requested and received dimensions, quality and number of images. Duration to result includes waiting; therefore it may differ from the time after launch.

The launch estimate and the confirmed costs are different values. If the service has not confirmed the charge, the amount is marked as estimated. The grand total above the list applies to the tasks shown; This is not the service account balance.

“Open” selects a specific completed image without new generation. Cancel and continue are separate card actions. Old unknown or interrupted jobs do not start from opening a list or starting another edit.

The archived record of the transferred project is available for reading; it does not continue the old cloud request or add the old expense to the new budget. If the outcome is unknown, check exactly the previous request before deliberately resubmitting it.

tour.tour.ui.intro: Explore the elements of this window in order, or choose a group. The guide explains the interface without starting photo processing.

tour.tour.ui.target-missing: The element could not be shown in the current window state. Its purpose is described here; you can move on to the next step.
tour.tour.ui.old-progress: The tour has changed and the previous step is no longer available. Choose a group or restart this window’s tour.
tour.tour.ui.progress-save-error: Your position in the tour could not be saved. You can keep reading, but this step may not be restored next time.

tour.busy-folder: The folder is still loading. Wait for it to finish before choosing it again or browsing its contents.
tour.no-folder: First, open your photos folder. After this, you can update its contents and file information.
tour.busy-action: The task is still being prepared or the command is already being executed. Wait for the result of the current action.
tour.process-selection: First, select the photos or folder to process.
tour.provider-not-ready: The selected processing method is not ready yet. The button shows the required action: install a local model, add or check a key. If the service is unavailable, the reason will be indicated next to it.
tour.copy-needs-smart-name: Creating a copy here is related to the smart name. To use this setting, first enable Smart Name.
tour.one-photo: This block refers to one photo. Select a photo in the workspace to see its details and available actions.
tour.photo-selection: Select photos. This editing block is not available for folders and regular files.
tour.selection-needed: Select the file, folder, or photo you want to view details about.
tour.rename-source: First, select the files or open the folder where you want to prepare the rename.
tour.history-back: There is no previous location in the navigation history yet. This button becomes available after you move between folders.
tour.history-forward: There is no next location in the navigation history. Use this button after going back.
tour.no-parent: You are at the root of the disk: there is no parent folder here. Another drive can be selected via the computer icon.
tour.folder-scope: To search the current folder, first open it. A search throughout the entire library is available using already saved information.
tour.no-search-results: Actions are specific to the search performed. First, set the conditions and click "Search".
tour.explorer-only: This element refers to the contents of the folder in Explorer. The search results use its own terms and order.
tour.table-only: Column selection is available in tabular form. When Table is enabled, the button is in its header.
tour.empty-content: There are no items available here yet. Open your photo folder or select a different collection.
tour.two-photos: To compare, select two photos, holding down Ctrl while selecting the second one.
tour.right-panel-hidden: The right panel is now hidden. In a narrow window, it is opened by the “Panel” button next to the view controls. There you will find information about the photo, description, tags and tasks.
tour.collection-target: Select photos and an existing collection. A new collection can be created using the line below.
tour.metadata-save: Saving is available when there are changes and the photo is available in the library. If the source information was updated during editing, check the new result first.
tour.manual-queue: Manual queues have an “Add here” purpose. Processing immediately uses the shared queue regardless of this choice.
tour.no-queue-items: There are no photos to display in this queue at this time. When “Hide completed” is enabled, completed items are not displayed. An empty manual queue can be filled with the “Add to queue” button.
tour.queue-selected: First, select the created task whose parameters you want to view.
tour.editor-busy: This command is not available during frame conversion or comparison. Return from comparison or wait for the conversion to complete, then repeat the action.
tour.brush-mode: This field works with the mask brush and eraser. Another tool is currently selected, so the tutorial shows the field disabled.
tour.two-history-frames: Comparison needs two images from the history. Hold Ctrl while selecting them when they are available.
tour.outpaint-mode: The frame and dimensions of the expansion refer to the Expand Image operation. They will appear when you select it yourself.
tour.no-markup: There are no points, areas or masks in the frame yet. They will appear in the list after the markup is created.
tour.no-mask-strokes: There are currently no unapplied mask strokes. Apply and cancel buttons appear as you work with them.
tour.instruction-targets: Choose a location for operations that accept instructions for individual annotations. Other operations use the whole-image instructions.
tour.model-without-text: In this version, the model does not use text instructions. Editing is determined by the supported markup and parameters.
tour.whole-image-references: A general block of additional images is visible when you select “Whole image” for a suitable operation and model. If a label is selected, it is hidden, saving attachments.
tour.mark-references: Additional images for an annotation are available for operations on points or areas. Masks do not have this attachment block.
tour.model-output: The composition of the result parameters depends on the model. Some options do not have a separate size or quality field.
tour.pending-outpaint-crop: The future frame cuts off part of the source. Apply pre-trimming first; then the following extension conditions will become available.
tour.editor-launch: Check the readiness of the task: the selected model, instructions or the required mask, key and acceptable rating. While editing is in progress, restarting is not available; the specific reason is shown in the editor.
tour.no-editor-jobs: Edits in this project have not yet been launched. After launch, a task card with its status and result will appear here.
tour.recoverable-editor-job: Continuation and reconciliation are available if the task was interrupted or it is unknown whether the service accepted it. For a completed task, you can open the finished result.
tour.running-editor-job: Cancellation is available for a running task. There is no need to cancel a completed edit as an active request.
tour.viewer-neighbors: There are no other photos available to flip through in the current set yet.
tour.slideshow-only: These controls appear during a slideshow. The tour does not start the slideshow automatically.

tour.tour.about.description: View and organize photos, create descriptions and tags, search your photo library, and edit images.
tour.tour.about.author: Author: {{author}}
tour.tour.about.tagline: Smart Photo Indexer — find the photos you need by what they show.
tour.tour.about.lead: Browse pictures in their familiar folders, add descriptions and tags, find images with words, and open them for editing. Process photos with a local model on your computer or through a configured cloud service.
tour.tour.about.step1.title: Open your folder.
tour.tour.about.step1.body: Browse photos as cards, a list, or a table. Mark favorites and organize pictures into collections.
tour.tour.about.step1.alt: Start with a familiar photo folder
tour.tour.about.step2.title: Add descriptions and tags.
tour.tour.about.step2.body: Choose your photos, model, and desired output. Process them immediately or build a queue first.
tour.tour.about.step3.title: Find a picture with words.
tour.tour.about.step3.body: Search saved descriptions, tags, filenames, and paths in the current folder or the whole library. Searching does not run recognition on unprocessed photos.
tour.tour.about.step3.alt: Search the saved contents with words
tour.tour.about.step4.title: View and edit your photo.
tour.tour.about.step4.body: Open the viewer to zoom in or start a slideshow. The editor offers cropping, resizing, and supported AI edits.
tour.tour.about.more: More useful tools. Photo comparison, batch tag editing, smart renaming, file operations, XMP, data backups, and editor projects.
tour.tour.about.requirements: Viewing does not require an AI key. Local recognition requires an installed model; cloud operations require your own key and may incur charges. Review model-generated descriptions, tags, and images.
tour.tour.about.license-pending: This project is licensed under Apache 2.0.

common.help: Explains what this section does and how to use its settings. Hover for a moment, or press “?” to keep the explanation open while reading. Press the button again or
common.close-dialog: Closes this settings or information window. To apply changes, use a separate save button, if available in the window.
common.dismiss-message: Removes the message from the screen. If it describes an error, its cause remains: check the status of the operation in the appropriate section.
common.cancel-draft: Cancels preparing changes to this form and returns to the previous screen. Already saved results remain.
common.reset-draft: Returns the last saved values to the fields. Use this if you want to discard changes that you have not yet saved.
common.expand: ”. Press again to collapse it. Opening the section does not start an operation.
common.page-prev: ". This is a navigation through the list entries, not a return to the previous photo.
common.page-next: ". Use to view entries that do not fit on the current page.
common.load-more: Loads the next part of the list "
common.retry-read: ” again after a reading error. This does not repeat a paid generation request.
common.acknowledge: Closes this message and returns to work.
common.copy-path: Copies the full path to this file to the clipboard. It can be pasted into Windows Explorer or message to indicate the location of the file.
common.reveal-file: Opens the file location in Windows Explorer. This way you can find the original on disk and work with it outside the program.
common.favorite-add: Marks a photo with a star and adds it to the “Favorites” section so you can quickly find it later. The file remains in the same place.
common.favorite-remove: Removes the star and removes the photo from the “Favorites” section. The photo and its description remain in the library.
common.minimize: Minimizes this window to the Windows taskbar. Click its icon to return to it. The window stays open.
common.maximize: Expands the window to view a larger area. Clicking again returns the window to its normal size.
common.restore: Returns the maximized window to its normal size. It can be moved and resized by the edges.
common.theme-dark: Switches the interface to dark colors. The setting affects the design of the program, not the colors of the photos.
common.theme-light: Switches the interface to light colors. The setting affects the design of the program, not the colors of the photos.
common.wait: ". Wait for the result of this operation.
common.no-selection: First, click on the photo you want to select it. To select multiple images, hold
common.splitter: Drag the border to resize adjacent areas. This helps you allocate more space to your photos or settings without changing the content.
common.window-menu: Opens the commands of this window. Select the desired action from the list; Opening the menu itself does not change anything.
text.bold: Makes selected words bold so they stand out in the description. First, select a piece of text, then click this button. To save the design along with the text, click “Save Description”.
text.italic: Makes the selected text italic. Use for small semantic accents in the description.
text.underline: Underlines the selected fragment of the description. The design change must be saved along with the text.
text.bullets: Formats the selected rows as a list with bullets. It is convenient to list several individual characteristics of a photograph.
text.numbered: Formats the selected rows as a numbered list. Use when the order of items is important.
text.undo: Undoes the last action in the current text editor. This does not cancel recognition or changes to the photo.
text.redo: Returns the action undone in the current text editor.
text.link: First, highlight the words that will become the link, then enter the HTTP or HTTPS address. The link will be part of the saved description.
text.link-address: Insert the full address of the page, starting with http:// or https://. It will be linked to the highlighted fragment of the description.
text.link-apply: Applies the specified address to the selected words. To save the edited description to the library, then click Save Description.
text.expand: Gives more space to read and edit the description. Pressing it again returns the compact view; the text does not change.
text.collapse: Returns a compact view of the description field. The typed text remains in the editor.
main.choose-folder: Opens a folder with photos and shows its contents in the app’s Explorer. Here you can view pictures, select them for recognition and open them in the editor.
main.refresh-folder: Rereads the contents of an open folder to show added, deleted, or modified files. Use if you changed files outside the program and the list has not yet been updated.
main.refresh-index: Checks information about files in the library index and updates their status. The index stores information for searching; this action itself does not trigger new AI recognition.
main.refresh-mode: Allows you to select the action of the main button: reread the open folder or check the index. The selected option is saved for future clicks.
main.provider: Choose where to recognize photo content: locally via Ollama or in the cloud via Fal AI/OpenRouter. For local mode, you need an installed model; for cloud mode, you need the key for the corresponding service.
main.model: Select a model to recognize photos in new tasks. The quality of descriptions and tags, speed of work and cost depend on it. Available models depend on the service selected.
main.output: Choose what information to receive when recognizing a photo.
- coherent text about the contents of the image.
- short words to search for, for example “cat”, “sofa”, “window”. The Description and Tags option saves both results.
main.output-description: Saves coherent text about what is shown in the photo. Already existing tags are not replaced by the result of this mode.
main.output-tags: Saves search words and expressions about a photo. For example: “dog”, “grass”, “walk”. The full description is not replaced by this mode.
main.output-both: Saves both text about the contents of the photo and short search tags. This information helps you find the snapshot using different queries.
main.recursive-process: Includes photos in subfolders at any depth. For example, select a trip folder to process pictures in its daily subfolders. This setting does not change the current list view.
main.smart-name: Renames the file using a date and a unique code. It uses the date taken from the metadata, or the file’s modification date if no date taken is available. The name does not come from the AI-generated description.
Enable Create copy to keep the original file under its current name.
main.analysis-copy: Keeps the original file and creates a separate copy with a smart name. This option requires Smart name; choose where to save copies in Settings.
main.copy-disabled: First, enable “Smart name”: this setting creates exactly a copy with a new smart name.
main.only-missing: Skips photos that already have all the requested results. If you request both a description and tags but only the tags are ready, the missing description is added. Failed or stopped work does not count as a completed result.
main.process-direct: Adds the selected photos to the general queue and starts processing. Photos that are already pending or being processed will not be added again.
With the “Unprocessed only” setting, the program skips already completed descriptions or tags, depending on the selected result.
main.process-manual: Adds selected photos to a manual queue
. If the queue has “Add here” enabled, the photos will go to it; otherwise a new one will be created.
This way you can prepare several collections, and then open “Tasks” and launch the desired queue.
main.process-mode: Choose whether to launch selected photos immediately or only add them to a manual queue. The main button label changes; Selecting the mode itself does not launch anything.
main.mode-direct: The main button will be called “Process”. The selected photos go to the general queue and processing starts.
main.mode-manual: The main button will be called “Add to Queue”. Prepare your photos, then open Tasks and separately run the desired manual queue.
main.add-key: Opens the key entry for the selected cloud service. The key associates requests with your service account; After saving and checking, you can start recognition.
main.check-key: Checks whether the service accepts the saved key and whether the selected model is available. If the test fails, the program will show the reason so you can correct the setting.
main.install-local: Prepares local recognition: the program will install the required component Ollama and download the selected model. The confirmation window shows the download volume and the required actions.
main.readiness-check: The availability of the selected service or local model is checked. Wait for the test result: after it, the button will offer processing or the necessary setting.
main.preparing: The program collects the selected photos and checks which of them need to be processed. Do not press again: the preparation result will appear in the queue.
main.service-unavailable: . Check the selected service, model and key; After eliminating the cause, repeat the test.
main.edit-photo: Opens one selected photo in the editor: you can crop the photo, resize it, or perform AI editing. For this button, select exactly one photo.
main.editor-projects: Opens a list of saved editor projects. Here you can find previously edited photos and continue working with their history.
main.rename: Opens renaming of selected files or files of the current folder without accessing the neural network. First set up the names and check the preview, then apply the changes.
main.settings: Opens a selection of services and models, keys, file storage and processing options. The settings for new jobs do not automatically overwrite already prepared queues.
main.logs: Shows application technical messages. They are useful in troubleshooting errors and freezes; This is a separate list from the photo changelog.
main.back: Returns to the previous browsing history folder. This is navigation through opened folders, and not canceling actions with a photo.
main.forward: Moves to the next history folder after returning with the Back button.
main.up: Opens the parent folder. For example, go from a folder for one day of a trip to the folder containing the whole trip.
main.breadcrumb: " in the current path. This way you can quickly move up several levels without repeatedly clicking “One level up”.
main.computer: Shows computer disks. Select the drive to open its root folder; then you can navigate through the subfolders.
main.tab-explorer: Shows the contents of an open folder. Select files to view, recognize, or edit.
main.tab-search: Opens a search with a separate query and detailed conditions: fields, tags, dates and other filters. It has its own terms, separate from the top quick search.
main.tab-favorites: Shows photos marked with a star. This is a convenient list of your favorite photos without moving files to another folder.
main.tab-ready: Shows photos with saved processing results. You can check descriptions and tags without searching for files in their original folders.
main.tab-collections: Opens your photo collections. A photo can belong to several collections without being moved or copied on disk.
main.tab-recent: Shows folders that you have already opened. Click the desired entry to quickly return to its content.
main.open-recent: " that you were looking at earlier. The program will show its current contents; this is not a saved copy of the file list.
main.refresh-results: Reruns the current query with the same conditions and sort. Use to see library changes; The order of the search list shown is maintained until updating.
main.refresh-results-dirty: Library data has changed since this list was received. Click to update the results and their order. The previously prepared queue retains its selected composition.
main.compare: Shows two selected photos for comparison.
and click on two photos, then click Compare. You can view them side by side or overlay them and move the dividing line to reveal different parts of each photo.
