parameter.background: Selects the background behavior, such as automatic, transparent, or opaque. Available options are for this model; transparency must also be supported by the format.
parameter.num-images: Sets the number of images to be retrieved per request. Several options may increase the cost; check the full run estimate.
parameter.seed: Sets the number from which the model starts generation. With the same source, number and other settings, you can try to get a similar option again. The service does not guarantee a completely identical image.
parameter.guidance: Adjusts the influence of the text task on generation. A higher value does not always give a better result; Use the acceptable range and recommendations of the selected model.
parameter.prompt-expansion: Allows the service to expand or clarify your text before generation. This may help the model, but added language may change the interpretation of the problem.
parameter.prompt-mode: Selects how the service improves the task text before generation.
reduces generation time. The parameter is available for models that support this refinement.
parameter.rendering-speed: Selects the execution mode supported by the model. The accelerated option may differ in detail and tariff; the score refers to the current choice.
parameter.thinking: Sets how much additional reasoning the model uses, where supported. It can affect processing time and cost, but does not guarantee better quality.
parameter.web-search: Allows the supporting model to refer to an Internet search when preparing a result. This feature may cost extra; turn it on only when necessary.
parameter.system: Specifies an additional control instruction for the model where the service supports it. This is a technical parameter, separate from the usual description of the desired edit.
parameter.safety: Selects the level of content filtering available in the scheme. The service rules continue to apply; the parameter does not guarantee the acceptance of any request.
parameter.limit-generations: Asks the model to create one image at each stage of work and ignore requests for several images in the text of the assignment. This is an experimental mode; it may affect the quality.
It does not replace the selection of the number of results or the editor's monetary budget.
parameter.style: Choose what visual style you want the model to create the result in. For example, the options available with this model can be designed for realistic photography or design. The list is determined by the selected model.
parameter.style-preset: Applies a pre-made style from model options. Check whether it is suitable for the task if it is important to preserve the photographic appearance of the source.
parameter.style-codes: Sets the style with special codes that this model supports. Each code consists of eight hexadecimal characters - the numbers 0-9 and the letters A-F. Use either codes or regular style selection; sharing these settings together is not supported.
parameter.palette: Sets the desired colors for models that support
. In the “JSON Parameters” you can specify a ready-made palette, for example
, or a list of colors in the model schema format. A ready-made palette and a custom list are not specified at the same time.
parameter.negative: Lists undesirable outcome features of models that support a negative instruction. This is a generation wish, and not an absolute ban on the appearance of an item.
parameter.prompt: Allows you to specify the desired result with text if the selected model mode accepts instructions. Describe what needs to be changed or kept. The availability of this option may vary by model.
parameter.preserve-alpha: Asks the model to preserve the transparent areas of the original image. Check the result and use a format with transparency when saving.
parameter.refine-foreground: Improves the separation of the front object from the calculated mask. Useful for object boundaries when removing background; the result depends on the model and source.
parameter.mask-only: Returns only a black and white object separation mask instead of a regular photo with the background removed. Refinement of object edges is skipped in this mode. Use when you need the mask itself.
parameter.output-mask: Asks the service to additionally return a mask that separates the object from the background. To replace the usual result with one mask, another setting is provided - “Mask only”.
parameter.mask-expansion: Extends the boundary of the processed mask by the specified number of pixels. A small margin may catch the edges of the object; too big will change the surrounding environment.
parameter.model-remove: Selects the object or background removal algorithm within this service. General, portrait and other options are intended for different sources; This is not a change in the main provider.
parameter.model-object-removal: Selects the level of processing of the deleted area: from
- the best in this service. Changing levels may affect price and time; the main editor service remains the same.
parameter.model-background: Selects the BiRefNet option: universal, portrait or designed for precise edge separation. Start with a universal option; check the object boundaries on the result.
parameter.model-precision: Selects the Topaz Precision option for the source: regular photo, low resolution, graphics, text or faces. The Text Refine option focuses on clarity of text and shapes.
parameter.model-generative: Selects the Topaz variant for generative detail restoration. Variants balance preserving the original image and recreating missing details differently. Compare the result with the original.
parameter.model-restore: Selects the Topaz recovery method. Recover 3 recreates details, Dust-Scratch V2 is designed to remove dust and scratches. These are different tasks for processing an old photograph.
parameter.operating-resolution: Defines the size at which the model calculates object separation. The larger option can more accurately handle high resolution, but is not available for all algorithms.
parameter.mode-outpaint: Selects the mode for adding new fields.
is focused on more accurate results,
is faster, but may be worse at continuing complex details. The size of the future canvas is specified by the frame and size fields.
parameter.upscale-mode: Select magnification by ratio or target resolution. In the first case, the multiplier of the sides is set, in the second - the required level of result.
parameter.upscale-factor: Specifies how many times to increase the width and height. For example,
turns 1000 × 600 into 2000 × 1200 pixels—both sides are doubled, and the total number of pixels quadruples.
parameter.target-resolution: Selects the final size level in target resolution mode. The available options and the preservation of proportions are determined by the model.
parameter.steps: Sets the number of model processing steps. More steps may increase the time and does not necessarily improve the result beyond a certain level.
parameter.creativity: Regulates the freedom of the model when restoring new parts. A high value may give more expressiveness, but will change the original features more.
parameter.resemblance: Controls how much the result should preserve features of the original image. Combine with finishing details if it is important to avoid unnecessary changes.
parameter.denoise: Controls the reduction of visual noise. Strong processing can smooth out the useful fine texture.
parameter.sharpen: Controls the emphasis of edges and fine details. Excessive sharpening can create ghosting and does not reliably restore missing detail.
parameter.fix-compression: Tries to reduce blocks and distortions resulting from strong file compression. This feature is not available for all modes of the selected model.
parameter.strength-text: Adjusts the strength of the enhancement in the Topaz Precision Model's Text Refine mode. This option does not set the weight of your text instruction and is not used in all zoom modes.
parameter.face: Includes special facial processing to enhance the visibility of details. The reconstructed features may differ from the real person, so compare the result with the original.
parameter.face-strength: Regulates the expression of facial processing. The stronger the transformation, the more carefully it is worth checking the safety of the original features.
parameter.face-creativity: Adjusts the freedom of the model when recreating facial details. Works when face restoration is enabled; high freedom can change appearance.
parameter.enhancement: Adjusts the degree of generative recovery in supported augmentation mode. If the parameter is not specified, the model can choose the value automatically.
parameter.subject: Selects a part of the image to automatically detect the object when enhancing:
- the entire image,
- the foreground,
- the background. It is taken into account only by model algorithms that support this choice.
parameter.noise-scale: The model uses this noise factor when generating the image. Start with the standard value. The service does not explain the exact visual effect of the parameter in the diagram, so changing it does not promise a certain degree of detail or similarity.
parameter.light-direction: Choose where you want the light to come from: left, right, top or bottom. The option without a given direction leaves this choice to the model.
parameter.cfg-light: Controls the effect of given light conditions when processed by this model. A higher value may change the scene more.
parameter.lowres-denoise: Adjusts the conversion force on the first, reduced machining pass. This is not the number of description recognition passes in the main program.
parameter.hr-fix: Includes an additional high-resolution processing pass. Its settings are made available separately and may increase execution time.
parameter.hr-downscale: Leave the default value at 0.5 unless you are customizing the IC-Light process. The service allows values ​​from 0.01 to 1, but does not explain the effect of the parameter in the published schema; the expected visual effect is not promised in advance.
parameter.highres-denoise: Adjusts the strength of changes in the additional high-resolution pass. Used only when the second pass is enabled.
parameter.enhance-resolution: Enables this model's resolution enhancement during recovery. The final dimensions need to be checked after receiving the result.
parameter.fix-colors: Enables processing of faded or distorted colors in an old photo. If you want to preserve the black and white character, also check the original color preservation setting.
parameter.remove-scratches: Includes treatment of scratches and damage to old photographs. The model can approximately restore the contents hidden by them.
settings.hover-hints: Shows explanations when you hover over or navigate to an element using the
key. Turn them off when no longer needed. The
buttons continue to open explanations when pressed. The selection is saved after the program is closed.
settings.recursive-view: Also shows photos of subfolders in Explorer. This is a list setting; bypassing subfolders during processing is enabled by a separate option “Subfolders” in the processing panel.
settings.images-only: Hides other files in the lists so that they do not interfere with the selection of photos. Files hidden by this filter are not deleted.
settings.cloud-consent: Maintains permission to send images to the selected cloud service and model provider. It is used both in recognition and in the editor; There is no need to re-confirm each launch as long as the permission is saved.
settings.request-delay: Adds a pause between recognition requests in milliseconds. May help comply with service restrictions, but increases overall uptime.
settings.job-budget: Sets the new job's spending limit in dollars.
. For a given limit, the program takes into account the estimate of requests and already known costs; the actual charge is reported by the service.
settings.retries: Sets the number of times the request will be repeated in case of temporary failures. This helps you continue working after a short-term connection or service problem.
An incorrect key must be corrected manually. If the outcome of a previous cloud request is unknown, reconciliation is required first to avoid resubmitting the same work.
settings.passes: In one pass, the model immediately produces a description or tags. If there are several, the program receives options, and in the last pass it double-checks them using a photograph.
More passes require more time and cloud requests; the number of passes does not apply to editing the image itself.
settings.concurrency: Limits the number of concurrent recognition requests. It's not the number of photos in the entire queue; the local model processes one photo at a time.
settings.pause-ai-error: Pauses the queue after a final recognition error so you can investigate the cause. When turned off, the remaining available photos continue to be processed.
settings.pause-rename-error: Suspends related work after a rename error. Useful if it is important to check file names and availability before proceeding.
settings.tokens: Limits the length of the model's complete response. Token is a small fragment of text; it is not equal to one word or sentence. The limit is spent on the description, tags and service structure of the response.
A value that is too low may cut off the response. The desired detail of the description is also specified by the model instructions.
settings.image-side: Limits the size of the image prepared for recognition. A smaller frame may be processed faster, but lose fine detail; the original file is not reduced.
settings.copy-destination: Choose to create copies next to the source or in a separate folder. This is a location for recognition copies, separate from the storage of editor projects.
settings.copy-choose: Specifies a folder for smartly named files when copying to the selected location is enabled. The original photos remain in their folders.
settings.photo-storage: Choose where to save the editor's results: as a new file next to the source or in a separate folder. You can also set the location to be selected each time you save.
settings.photo-folder: Specifies the folder for the editor's finished images. This is a setup for future saves, not a transfer of all previous exported files.
settings.project-storage: Projects store working images and editor history, while the cache stores temporary viewing data. These vaults are carried separately from the original photos and general Ollama models.
settings.move-projects: Moves the editor's project storage to the selected location and checks the copy. Before transferring, close the editor; The old folder is retained for testing.
settings.move-cache: Moves the cache storage to the selected folder. This helps place temporary data on another drive without moving photos and projects.
key.input: Insert the API key from the personal account of the selected service. Using this key, the service identifies your account and allows requests from the program. The Fal AI key is suitable for Fal AI, the OpenRouter key is suitable for OpenRouter.
key.paste: Substitutes text from the clipboard into the key field. Make sure that you copied the key for the desired service, then save it.
key.show: Temporarily displays the entered characters to verify insertion. If there are other people nearby or your screen is being recorded, use hidden input.
key.hide: Masks the entered key in the field. Hiding characters does not delete the key or prevent it from being saved.
key.save: Remembers the entered key for the selected service. Checking the connection and starting recognition are performed separately; this press only saves the key.
key.save-check: Saves the entered key and checks the readiness of the service. After successful verification, you can return to processing without re-entering.
key.check-saved: Checks the already added key and access to the selected model. There is no need to enter a new key if the saved one remains valid.
key.check-service: Checks the connection and access of the selected service with the current key. This is a readiness check, not a photo edit.
local.endpoint: Indicates where the program should contact Ollama. To work on the same computer,
is usually used. If Ollama is configured with a different address, enter it here; This is not a link to download the model.
local.check: Checks whether Ollama is available and the selected model is installed. If something is missing, use the model setup.
local.setup: Prepares Ollama and the selected local model automatically. Before starting, the loading plan and volume are shown; The first launch requires time, internet and free space.
local.confirm-install: Launches the shown plan: the program itself will install the necessary components Ollama and download the selected model. Wait for it to be ready and return to processing. There is no need to enter commands in the terminal.
local.installing: The program loads and prepares local components. Follow the stage and progress shown; repeating the command does not speed up loading.
local.cancel-install: Interrupts the current preparation or loading of a model. Already existing photos and library information are not affected. You can restart the preparation later.
local.ready: The selected local model is ready for use. Recognition is performed on this computer; The time depends on the model, image size and computer resources.
local.setup-capsule: Shows the readiness of the selected model and the available preparation action. If the model is not yet installed, click to configure and read the download plan.
cloud.check-capsule: Shows the key and availability status of the selected cloud model. Pressing performs a check and does not recognize the selected image.
recovery.section: Allows you to replace the key of a saved task and check the outcome of previous requests. Already paid known answers are restored separately from the new launch.
recovery.fal: Checks the states of saved Fal requests with the service. This is a check of previously submitted work, without creating new generation requests.
consent.continue: Saves the cloud send permission and continues the action for which the issue is open. Please read what images will be transferred before confirming.
rename.about: Explains how new names are constructed and how to test them before writing them down. Renaming changes the file name, not the content of the photo, and does not require an AI request.
rename.names: Opens rules and previews of new names. Set up the base, extensions and numbering, then check the result.
rename.history: Shows previous rename operations and available actions to continue or revert names. This is a different history from image editing.
rename.operation: Shows the saved rename operation: status, time and number of files. Select it to check the result and available actions.
rename.prefix: Adds text before the main part of the name. For example, the prefix “Vacation” helps to unite files with a common theme. Check the full name in the preview.
rename.base: Choose to keep the same name or have a common base for all selected files. Numbering helps distinguish files with a common basis.
rename.common: Enter the main part of the new name, for example "Product". If there are several files, check the numbering and possible matches in the preview.
rename.suffix: Adds text after the main part of the name. It can indicate an option or a group of shots; The file extension is processed separately by the program.
rename.numbering: Adds a sequential number to names. This allows you to distinguish between multiple files with a common basis. Position, start and pitch are adjustable side by side.
rename.number-position: Selects whether the number will appear before or after the main part of the name. Check the resulting order in the preview.
rename.start: Specifies the number of the first file in the sequence. For example, starting with 101 allows you to continue the existing numbering.
rename.digits: Adds leading zeros to the desired length: for example, 001 instead of 1. Without leading zeros, the number is written in the usual way.
rename.order: Determines the order in which files are numbered: as listed, by name, or by date modified. This is important before applying numbering.
rename.separator: Selects a character between parts of the new name: underscore, hyphen, space, or no separator. The full result is visible in the preview.
rename.recursive: Adds subfolder files to this rename operation. This is a custom setting for this window, separate from viewing and AI processing of subfolders.
rename.step: Sets how much to increase the next file number. For example, starting with 1 and step 2 will result in numbers 1, 3, 5.
rename.per-folder: Restarts numbering within each folder. Without this setting, the counter follows the general order of the operation.
rename.apply: Gives new names to files ready to be renamed in preview. Please check the displayed names, matches and errors before running. The content of the photos remains the same.
rename.resume: Continues an unfinished saved operation in its log. This is not creating a new naming scheme from scratch.
rename.rollback: Restores the previous names from the unfinished operation’s log. A complete rollback may be impossible if files were later moved or renamed outside the app.
rename.restore-names: Uses the log of the selected operation to revert available files to their previous names. Before performing, check which operation you have chosen.
rename.preview-cancel: Removes prepared name variants without using them. You can change the settings and check the new result.
rename.preview-confirm: Confirms the names shown and continues the action for which the preview was opened: processing or preparing a queue. This confirmation is only required for public preview; The "Process" mode does not ask it before each launch.
help.open: Opens tour for the current window and reference book. You can search for the function you need or ask the program to show its location.
help.tour-tab: Opens a step-by-step introduction to the elements of the current window. The program shows where the function is and explains its purpose.
help.reference-tab: Opens articles explaining the program's capabilities. You can read the material without going through all the steps of the tour.
help.hints-reveal: Pulls out the tooltip toggle. The checkbox turns on or off explanations when hovering over program elements.
help.hints-toggle: Enables or disables explanations when hovering over program elements. When the checkbox is unchecked, other tooltips do not appear.
help.group: Limits tour to the selected topic. "All sections in this window" returns the full set of available functions.
help.feature: Selects a specific function to explain and display in the current window. Item unavailability may depend on the selected photo or job status.
help.all: Begins familiarizing yourself with all available training steps in this window. Processing actions do not trigger from just showing tooltips.
help.continue: Returns to the next available step of getting to know the interface.
help.group-start: Starts tour only on the selected topic, such as search or queuing.
help.groups: Returns to the list of tour topics to select a different program area.
help.step-prev: Shows the previous training step. This is not undoing the photo action.
help.step-next: Shows the next tour step. The final step, “Done” completes the tour.
help.search: Searches for help articles based on the entered words. This is a search for explanations of functions, not a search for photographs.
help.article: Opens the selected article describing the feature. To show its place in the interface, use the associated tour commands.
help.show-feature: " in the program and its explanation. Demonstration does not automatically perform this function.
help.screenshot: Opens the illustration larger to see the arrangement of elements. This is a reference shot and not an image of your current photo.
preview.gestures: The mouse wheel zooms in or out. After zooming in, hold down the left button and drag the photo to view another area. Double-clicking again shows the entire image, selecting the appropriate scale.
compare.pan: Enlarge the photo, hold down the left button and drag it to view the desired area. In Side by Side mode, you can move the left and right images independently. The photos themselves do not change.
layout.panel-width: Drag the border left or right to change where you place your photos and settings. If the handle is selected from the keyboard, it can be moved using the arrows;
layout.markup-height: Drag the border to give more or less space to the markup list. Double clicking returns automatic height.
layout.editor-split: Drag the divider to resize adjacent areas of the editor. This is an adjustment to the layout of the panels, not the size of the image.
layout.column-width: Drag a column border to reveal more text. Double-clicking returns the default width of that column.
geometry.frame: Drag the frame or its handles to set the position and dimensions of the current crop or transform. Check the values ​​on the right and apply the result with a separate button.
markup.open-on-canvas: In selection mode, double-click an existing mark to open its assignment next to the canvas. Then you can change the description and additional pictures.
search.status-all: Does not limit search to processing state. The remaining terms of the request remain in effect.
search.status-ready: Shows photos with the status “Processed”: the recognition result has already been saved for them. These can be just the tags, just the description, or both. The missing fields can be retrieved with the "Unprocessed only" setting.
search.status-queued: Shows photos marked as pending or in processing. See the progress of a specific task in the “Tasks” tab.
search.status-not-ready: Limits the result to photos with the “Not processed” status. To run only missing results, use a separate "Unprocessed only" setting.
search.status-error: Shows photos with error status. Check the reasons and availability of restart in the tasks; the filter itself does not repeat the request.
search.status-missing: Shows photos whose file is not found in the saved path. Check the drive connection and last known location.
search.status-relocated: Shows entries for which the library has detected a path change. This is the file's location status, separate from the date it was taken or the contents of the image.
main.folders-first: Places folders before files, maintaining the selected sorting within groups. This makes it easier to select subfolders first.
main.folders-last: Places files before folders, maintaining the selected sorting within groups.
main.folders-mixed: Removes a separate grouping of folders. Folders and files participate in the general list order according to the selected sorting.
main.fit-fill: Fills the entire card with the photo. Part of the image at the edges can be hidden only in the preview; the original file is not cropped.
main.fit-contain: Shows the entire photo in the card while maintaining its proportions. If the shape of the card and the photo do not match, there will be empty fields.
main.view-table: Shows files in rows with properties: size, dates, status and other selected columns. You can change the width and composition of the columns.
main.view-list: Shows photos in compact lines with previews and details. Convenient for viewing names and a large number of files.
main.view-size: Selects thumbnail size from small to extra large. The larger the card, the better the details are visible and the fewer photos can fit at once.
main.no-folder-refresh: First open the folder. The refresh button refers to its content or index; it does not scan all drives itself.
main.edit-one-required: Select one photo to edit. To compare two photos, select them from
main.process-empty: Select the photos or folders you want to process. In the search, you can select results; prepared fields with “Unprocessed only” enabled will be skipped.
queue.concurrency-disabled: For a local model, one photo is taken at a time. For a completed or stopped job, the limit is no longer editable; For another queue, select its summary.
reference.unsupported: No additional images are used for this operation and model. Please select a compatible model if you would like to include a picture with the instructions; saved project attachments do not need to be deleted for viewing.
reference.point-replace: The dot uses one additional image. The new will replace it; To attach multiple pictures, use the model-supported general instruction or area.
model.filtered-empty: No model meets the selected conditions. Loosen the restrictions on price, size, or number of images, or reset the filters. The edit has not been submitted yet.
model.filter-loading: The program checks which models are suitable for your conditions and calculates the cost of editing with current parameters. Wait for the result, then apply the selection. The check is performed without generating an image.
model.launch-error: . Correct the specified parameter, instruction, key or image composition, then restart.
geometry.pending-crop: The entire original photo does not fit into the selected frame. Click Apply Crop to prepare a smaller frame, or change the size and position of the frame. Then you can set the margins for additional drawing.
geometry.invalid-size: Specify the final width and height as integers from 1 to 2048 pixels. You can add up to 1024 pixels on each side.
These are the customization limits of the extension frame. If the model returns different dimensions, its usable result is still preserved.
key.wait: The selected key is now being saved or verified. Wait for the response so as not to confuse the status of the previous and new input.
files.copy: Stores selected photos for copying inside Smart Photo. Open the desired folder in the program and select "Paste" or click
. The original files will remain in place. Before the new command, you can insert this set again.
files.cut: Remembers selected photos for moving. Then open the destination folder and click
. Before insertion, the files remain in the same place; The "Cut" command itself does not delete anything.
files.paste-copy: Copies saved photos to an open folder. The current selection in the grid does not change the prepared set. If the name is already taken, you can replace the file, save both with different names, or skip the conflict.
files.paste-move: Moves saved photos to an open folder. After a successful transfer, the source files move out of the previous folder. If some files could not be transferred, the program will report this separately.
files.copy-to: Opens the folder selection and copies the selected photos there. You can select a destination without leaving your current folder or search results. Deselecting does not change the files.
files.move-to: Opens the folder selection and transfers the selected photos there. After a successful transfer, descriptions, tags and links in the library are saved. If the name is busy, the program will offer options for this conflict.
files.trash: Sends the selected photos to the Windows trash bin. They can be restored from the recycle bin in the usual way. If sending to trash is not available, the program will report an error and will not replace it with permanent deletion.
files.drag-move: and drag a photo onto the destination folder. If the photo belongs to a selected group, all selected photos move together. Without
, dragging still draws a selection rectangle.
cancels the drag before you release the mouse button.
files.replace: Replaces a file in the destination folder with the selected photo. The previous contents of the target file will be replaced, so compare the specified paths. This selection does not trigger recognition or change other files with similar names.
files.replace-source-disabled: This file is also included in the selected source set. It cannot be replaced during this operation. Choose "Save Both" or "Skip" to avoid losing the selected photo.
files.keep-both: Keeps the existing file and saves the selected photo under an available name, such as “Photo (1).jpg”. The number is added before the extension; other files are not renamed.
files.skip: Skips this conflict without changing either file, then continues with the remaining photos. For a move, the skipped original stays in its current folder.
files.apply-all: Uses the selected option for the remaining conflicts of this operation. The next time you make a separate copy or move, the program will prompt you again for a choice. A target file that has changed after confirmation requires a new solution.
files.cancel-remaining: Does not start the following files in this set. Already completed actions are saved; This is not a cancellation of a previously completed copy or transfer. The currently started file phase may first complete safely.
settings.language: Choose the language of the application. Labels, hints and guided tours update in the main window, editor and viewer. The application remembers your choice for the next launch.
Changing the interface language does not translate your descriptions, tags or file names. The language used by AI to describe photos is selected separately.
tour.main.folder.refresh: Updates information about the open folder. The selected refresh mode determines what happens; its name appears on the button.
checks the folder’s contents again. Use it after adding, deleting or moving files outside the app.
updates the library’s information about those files. Generate new descriptions and tags by starting photo processing separately.
tour.main.folder.refresh-options: The arrow lets you choose between refreshing the folder and refreshing its index. Your choice becomes the action of the adjacent button.
To see changes made in Windows Explorer, refresh the folder. To generate a new description or new tags, start photo processing instead.

children: what you get as a result

tour.main.recognition.overview: . These decisions are related: each service has its own set of models, and the result can be a description, tags, or both.
First select the service, then the model and the required information. The processing conditions and the start button are to the right.
tour.main.recognition.output: - coherent text about what is visible in the photograph.
are short words and expressions that can be used to conveniently search for a photo. You can choose only one type of information or get both.

For example, for a photograph by the sea, the description will tell about the people, coastline and lighting, and the tags could be “sea”, “beach”, “sunset”. This selection also determines which results are considered ready when skipping processed photos.
tour.main.processing.overview: These controls prepare the selected photos for recognition. On the left, choose whether to include subfolders, use smart names and copies, or skip results that are already complete. The button on the right carries out the selected action.
adds photos to the shared queue and starts processing;
collects a separate batch without starting it. Choose the mode using the arrow beside the button.
tour.main.processing.recursive: Enable this option to process photos in subfolders as well as in the selected folder. With it turned off, subfolders are excluded.
Before starting a large folder, check which photos are included and the estimated cost. Subfolders may contain far more images than you can see at the current level.
tour.main.processing.action: This button uses the selected photos and folders.
adds them to the shared queue and starts processing; photos already waiting or being processed are not duplicated.
adds the selection without starting it, using the chosen manual queue or creating one if no destination is selected.
Queue contents and progress appear in Tasks on the right.
If the button asks you to install a model or add an API key, prepare that service first. Checking… means the app is checking whether it is ready.
tour.main.processing.mode: In this menu you select what the main button does:
. After selection, the button label also changes so that the action is visible before pressing.
Process uses the shared queue. Manual queues let you prepare several separate groups of photos, then start them from Tasks.
tour.main.commands.overview: This part of the top toolbar opens the photo editor, renaming tools, settings and technical logs. On the right, you can change the theme and open Help.

These commands solve different problems: the editor changes the image, renaming works with the file name, and the settings determine the operating conditions of the program. Next, let's look at each one in order.
tour.main.commands.edit: Opens the selected photo in the editor. There you can change the image itself: for example, crop it, adjust the size, or prepare an edit using a model.
Recognition generates descriptions and tags; the editor changes the image itself. Start the editor’s own tour from Help inside that window.
tour.main.commands.rename: Opens renaming of selected files or files in the current folder according to the rules. New names can be prepared and a preliminary list can be checked before use.
This command does not send photos to a model. Use it when you already know how you want to name the files.
tour.main.commands.settings: Here you configure recognition services, local processing and conditions for new tasks. You can also turn tooltips on and off in the settings.
Changing the settings of new tasks should not be confused with managing an already created queue: its parameters are shown separately in the “Tasks” tab.
tour.main.commands.logs: Opens the application's technical messages. They help you figure out at what stage the problem arose and convey the details when asking for help.
The history of actions on photos is separate, under Activity log in the right panel.
tour.main.commands.theme: Switches the appearance of the program between light and dark themes. The selection is saved and applied to program windows.
The theme changes the design of the interface; the colors of the photographs themselves remain the same.
tour.main.help.overview: explains the current window in order.
lets you find a topic and read about it separately.
The main window, editor and viewer each have their own tour. Open Help in the window you want to learn about.
tour.main.help.hover: A slide-out tooltip switch sits beside the question mark. Open it with the arrow to turn hover explanations on or off.
This switch and the option in Settings stay in sync. Turning tooltips off leaves the ? Help button available. The switch’s own tooltip also remains available so you can turn explanations back on.
tour.main.navigation.overview: Use this row to move between folders. On the left are the navigation-history buttons and the button for going up one level. Beside them are the drive selector and the current folder path.
History and the path serve different purposes. The arrows revisit locations you have already opened; the path segments let you jump directly to a particular level.
tour.main.navigation.back: Returns to the previous location in the navigation history. This may be a completely different folder than the parent folder of the current one.
If there is nowhere to return yet, the button is not available. After going back, you can go back forward using the adjacent arrow.
tour.main.navigation.forward: Returns to the next location in your navigation history after you have gone back. The button is available only when there is a location to return to.
To open the parent folder, use the up arrow instead of the history buttons.
tour.main.navigation.up: Opens the folder containing the current one. For example, from the “Vacation” folder inside “Photos” you will go to “Photos”.
At a drive’s root there is no parent folder. Use the computer icon to choose another drive.
tour.main.navigation.computer: The computer icon opens a list of available drives. Select a drive to go to its root folder and continue navigation from there.
opens the root of the C: drive. If the required removable or network drive is not available, first check its connection.
tour.main.navigation.breadcrumbs: This shows the path to the open folder, divided into parts. Click on the name of one of the previous levels to go directly there.
The last segment is the current folder, so it may not be clickable. To browse a neighboring folder, first open the appropriate parent level.
tour.main.quick.overview: This line helps you quickly find photos using saved information. Select your search area and fields, then enter your words - the results will update after a short pause.
Quick search is independent of the Search tab below. Use that tab to build more detailed search conditions and save them for reuse.
tour.main.quick.scope: limits the search to the selected folder and its subfolders. If another path is saved in the area, it is indicated as
searches among photographs for which the program already has information.
Searching the entire library does not mean going through all the disks again. To find photos by description or tags, you must first save this information.
tour.main.quick.fields: . You can leave several fields or limit the search to one.
For example, the word “sea” can be searched in descriptions and tags, and the folder name can be searched in the path. If all fields are turned off, search is not available: check at least one first.
tour.main.quick.query: Enter the word or expression you expect to find in the selected fields. For example, "red car", a file name or part of a path.

The search begins after a short pause in the input so that the program does not do unnecessary work for each letter. The result depends on the information already stored: the model does not look at the photos anew with each request.
tour.main.quick.actions: button explicitly starts a search for the current line and selected fields. The cross clears the top query and returns the normal contents of the workspace.
Clearing this request does not remove photos, descriptions, or tags. The terms on the individual Search tab apply to a different search.
tour.main.workspace.overview: Here you can switch between folders, search, favorites and ready photos, collections and recent folders. Explorer shows the files of the open folder; Search and collections help you find images based on information stored in the library.
First, we’ll look at the tabs and their contents, then we’ll look at display, sorting, and working with photos.
tour.main.workspace.explorer: Explorer shows the contents of an open folder. Here you can navigate to subfolders, select photos, and open them for viewing or editing.
Folders are located before files. You can limit the list to photos or show all files - this switch is located on the right above the contents of the folder.
tour.main.search.overview: This tab helps you collect a selection based on several conditions: words, tags, processing status, and dates. A convenient set of conditions can be saved and used again.
Unlike the top quick search, here you prepare the conditions and click
. If you change the filters after this, the results already shown may refer to the previous conditions - pay attention to the change mark.
tour.main.search.sections: tab you set a new search. The
tab contains sets of conditions that you have already given names.
The nearby star saves the current search conditions under a name you choose. Running that saved search later can return different photos, for example after new matching images have been added.
tour.main.search.query: Choose where and in what fields to search, enter the words and click
. You can search by description, tags, file name or path, as in the top line.
The reset button clears the terms of this search. It doesn't delete photos or erase saved descriptions or tags.
tour.main.search.primary-filters: The status filter helps you select, for example, completed photos or entries with errors. In the adjacent field you can specify tags separated by commas.
finds photos with at least one of the listed tags.
requires every listed tag to be present on the photo. These filters apply alongside the main query.
tour.main.search.additional: Additional filters can limit results to favorites, photos without tags, a collection or another folder. You can also choose whether to match word forms and synonyms.
The terms apply together, so check that they are not mutually exclusive. For example, searching for specific tags along with the “No tags” condition will not provide the desired selection.
tour.main.search.dates: to take into account: file change, shooting using camera data, adding to the index, or last recognition. Then set the start and end of the period.

These are different events. For example, a photograph could have been taken a long time ago, but a description for it could have been received today. To find recently recognized pictures, select the recognition date.
tour.main.search.saved: These are searches saved under names you chose. Select an entry to restore its conditions, adjust them if needed, then run the search.
The list can be filtered by name, and frequently used entries can be marked with a star. Renaming or deleting a saved search only changes that entry, not the photos.
tour.main.search.result-actions: This button opens actions with the results of the search performed. Inside, you can select an area: selected photos or the entire selection found, including results outside the current page.
Check the area before action. Search terms that have been changed but not yet applied do not mean that the selection already shown has been rearranged.
tour.main.search.results: The number of photos found belongs to the last completed search. Large result sets load progressively, so fewer photos may currently be visible than the total found.
You can select photos from the results, open them and process them. The new changes flag prompts you to update the results to take into account information that appears after the search.
tour.main.workspace.favorites: Photos marked with a star are collected here. This mark helps you quickly return to the desired pictures from different folders.
To remove a photo from your favorites, remove the star. The file itself and its description remain in place.
tour.main.workspace.ready: This tab shows photos with saved recognition results. It helps you return to the descriptions and tags you have already received and evaluate their quality.

Having one result does not always mean that everything you need is ready. For example, a photo may have tags without a description; When processing with the “Unprocessed only” setting, the selected result type is taken into account.
tour.main.workspace.collections: A collection is a named group of photos that may come from different folders. Use it to gather images for a purpose, such as Print or a Trip.
Adding to a collection does not move or copy files. One photo can be included in several collections. A convenient way to add selected pictures is also in the “Details” of the right panel.
tour.main.workspace.recent: Here you can quickly return to folders that you opened before. The entry shows the name and path to distinguish between folders with the same name.
This list records folders you visited. If a drive is disconnected or a folder has moved, its old path may no longer work. The history entry does not restore missing files.
tour.main.display.overview: These controls determine how thumbnails fit their cells, which list view to use, how files are sorted and which file types are shown.
Use them to make the current folder or search results easier to browse. In a narrow window, the group can switch to compact icons; the commands keep the same purpose.
tour.main.display.fit: fills the entire thumbnail cell; Some edges of the photo may not be included in the preview.
shows the entire photo, leaving space around it if necessary.
The selection only applies to thumbnails. The image in the file is not cropped.
tour.main.display.view: Select a table, list, or cards of the appropriate size. The table is convenient for comparing information, and large cards are useful for viewing the contents of photos.
Switching the view does not change the files themselves. The size of the cards can also be changed using the slider in the bottom line.
tour.main.display.columns: In a table view, you can choose which information to display in separate columns. The column selection button opens the list; Mark the ones you want and click
Settings help you leave useful data in the table.
returns the default set, and cancel closes the selection without applying the prepared changes.
tour.main.display.sort: Sorting controls the order of photos.
uses the file’s modification time, and
uses the time recognition results were successfully saved. Newest and oldest reverse the order.

You can also sort by name or type, or put completed photos and errors first or last. Explorer always places folders before files. Search results have their own relevant options, including relevance to the query.
tour.main.display.files: leaves images and folders for working with your photo library.
also shows the remaining files in the open folder.
Pictures are opened by our viewer, and other files are opened by the application assigned to them in Windows. This switch is specific to Explorer; Photo search uses an image library.
tour.main.display.filename: This filter helps to leave files with the appropriate name in the current folder. It's useful when you remember part of a title and want to quickly narrow down the visible list.
Search by description and tags is above. The name filter does not ask the model to recognize the content of photos.
tour.main.canvas.overview: This is where the contents of the selected folder or collection are located. First, select the elements you want, then use the process, view, or other appropriate action.
Selecting and dragging into a folder are different: normal mouse movement helps to select, and moving photos starts with holding down
. We'll look into the details further.
tour.main.canvas.selection: Click a photo to select it. To select several separate photos, hold
while clicking each one. Clicking a selected photo again while holding
You can also select elements by moving the mouse while holding down the left button. The selected photos are used by subsequent commands, so look at the selection counter before running.
tour.main.canvas.open: Double clicking on a photo opens the viewer, and on the folder - its contents. In the viewer, you can view the photo and move to adjacent photos of the available set.
When show all files is enabled, double-clicking on another file type opens it via Windows. There is a separate editor command for changing photos.
tour.main.canvas.context: Right-click to open the menu for the selected items. It puts relevant commands next to the items you are working with.
The available actions depend on whether you selected a photo, another file, a folder or several items.
tour.main.canvas.drag: To drag selected photos into a folder, hold
as you begin dragging. Then the mouse movement moves the pictures, rather than changing the selection. Release them over the desired folder.
If the action has not yet been performed,
cancels the dragging. If the names match, the program will offer to resolve the conflict; the selection can be applied to multiple matches.
tour.main.canvas.compare: Select two photos: click on the first one, then hold
and click on the second one. After this, the comparison command will become available.
The command opens both photos side by side so you can compare them. This differs from finding exact duplicates: the library’s duplicate check automatically groups identical files.
tour.main.footer.status: The bottom line shows the number of elements and their status: ready, in queue, not yet processed, or error. Nearby are information about the current selection.

For one photo you can see the format, resolution and size. For multiple items, a general summary is displayed; The contents of the folders are counted in the background. While the calculation is not completed or part of the data is unavailable, the program reports this, rather than passing off an incomplete size as an accurate one.
tour.main.footer.view: The slider switches the view from table and list to cards of different sizes. Move it if you want to see more files at once or take a closer look at the thumbnails.
This scale refers to the list. To enlarge the photo itself, open it in the viewer.
tour.main.inspector.overview: The right panel helps you work with the selected photo and monitor its processing. This contains file information, description, tags, queues, library data and action history.
First, let's look at the tabs, then their contents from top to bottom. For descriptions and tags, selecting the photo on the left is important; tasks and library are available without this choice.
tour.main.inspector.tabs: show information about the selected item,
show saved results and their editing.
Switching tabs helps you see a different type of information. To select another photo, click on it in the work area or in the list of queue items.
tour.main.details.overview: Here you can check which file is selected, where it is located and what information is known about it. Previews and related actions are available for the photo.
When you select multiple items, the information changes. General data about the selection, including size, can also be viewed in the bottom line of the main window.
tour.main.details.preview: The preview helps you recognize the selected photo. Next to it, you can open a photo for viewing, navigate to its location, or open the editor if you need to change the image.
The star adds the photo to Favorites. Edit its description and tags in the neighboring tabs of the right panel.
tour.main.details.file-info: The information helps you differentiate between similar files by checking the name, path, type, size, and available image data. The set of lines depends on the selected element and what was read from the file.
An unknown value means that the program does not yet have this information. It is not replaced by an assumption of size or date.
tour.main.details.collections: This block adds selected photos to named collections. The top line selects an existing collection, the bottom line creates a new one.
Collections help you combine pictures from different folders without moving files. The selected collection is remembered, so you can select new photos one by one and add them to one collection.
tour.main.details.collection-add: Select a collection from the list and click
to include the selected photos. Selecting from the list by itself does not add pictures.
The labels below show which collections contain the selected photos. Removing a collection link removes the photos from that collection while keeping their files on disk.
tour.main.details.collection-create: Enter a meaningful name and click plus to create a collection. The new entry will appear in the list and will be selected for future additions.
Creating a collection and adding photos are different actions. Once created, click
if you want to include the current selection.
tour.main.description.overview: A description explains what is visible in the photo. You can generate one through recognition, then refine it in your own words.
Here you work with the text of the selected photo. If there is no description, start typing your text in the empty field and save it.
tour.main.description.edit: Enter or edit a description. In the panel above the field, you can highlight important words, create a list, or add a link to the selected piece of text.
Undo and redo help you correct your edits. Expanding the field gives you more room for long text; you still need to save your changes with the save button.
tour.main.description.save: to record your changes to the selected photo.
returns the field to its saved state, discarding the current unsaved edits.
If information about the photo has changed during editing, the program reports this. Check the current text first to avoid overwriting newer results.
tour.main.tags.overview: Tags are short words and expressions that help you find photos and collect collections. For example: “forest”, “autumn”, “walk”.
For one photo, you can change its tags individually. For several photos below, there is a common block: it allows you to add new tags and remove unnecessary ones right from the selection.
tour.main.tags.single: Enter tags separated by commas. The current set is shown as separate tiles; The cross removes the tag from the editable set.
tour.main.tags.batch-overview: This block applies changes to selected photos. You can enter tags to add and mark existing tags to remove, then save both changes together.
The operation is designed for a set of up to
. Linked copies of the same photo share information, so changing its tags applies to them as well.
tour.main.tags.batch-add: Enter the words separated by commas that you want to add to all selected photos. For example, for snapshots of one trip, you can add the location and name of the event.
The new tags will complement the existing ones, preserving the remaining words for each photo. To remove a previous tag, check it below; then apply the prepared changes with the
tour.main.tags.batch-remove: Here are the tags found in the selected photos. Not every photo necessarily has a tag on this list.
. By pressing again you can remove the check mark before saving. When applied, the tag will be removed from those selected photos that have it.
tour.main.tags.batch-save: simultaneously adds the entered tags and removes the selected ones. Before clicking, make sure the photos you want are selected on the left.
After a successful change, a command to cancel the last operation with tags appears. It refers to the batch change performed, not the entire processing history.
tour.main.tags.xmp: saves descriptions and tags in separate files beside the photos. Transfer those files along with the photos, then use
in the app on the other computer.

per transaction. If a different description is found during import, the program reports a conflict and keeps the existing text without silent replacement. The transfer of the entire library, collections and projects is located separately - in the “Program Data” block.
tour.main.queue.overview: In the “Tasks” tab you can see which photos are prepared for recognition, what is being done and what results have already been obtained. Here you can continue working after a pause and check errors.
Processing immediately uses the shared queue. Manual queues store individual collections that you have collected using the “Add to queue” button. These are shown in the drop-down cards below.
tour.main.queue.controls: The main button changes depending on the operating status: allows you to start, pause or continue. Pausing saves the remaining work; stopping terminates the current run. Erroneous photos can be repeated using the available repeat command.

During general startup, prepared queues are executed sequentially: after one, the program moves on to the next. An empty queue does not create work. If the queue is waiting for the previous one, this can be seen from its state.
tour.main.queue.cost: The estimate shows the expected cost before processing. Confirmed spending shows known charges for completed requests. The two amounts can differ.

Cost depends on the service, model and task settings. Local processing and cloud requests are accounted for differently. Waiting for the service or for a status check does not mean the work is complete.
tour.main.queue.progress: Overall progress shows the status of the current job, and counters help distinguish between ready, pending, and failed items. The details of a particular photo are in its row within the queue.
An error on one photo and a user pause are different states. Error handling also depends on the task settings. Read the error message to see what can be retried or corrected.
tour.main.queue.list: Open the card to see the included photos. The header shows the number of shots, the number of completed ones and the work status; Clicking on the name displays the parameters of this queue in a summary, without launching it.
removes the completed item from display, and
returns it. This filter does not delete results and does not hide erroneous elements as ready ones.
tour.main.queue.card-actions: The start button in the card starts or continues this particular queue. A trash can in a card removes it from the work list, and a trash bin in the general header clears all recognition work queues.
These actions do not delete originals or already saved results. They change planned work; expense history is saved.
tour.main.queue.photo: Click on the thumbnail or name to select that photo and see its details on the right. Double-clicking opens the photo in the editor.
The line shows the operating status and available error details. The trash bin on the right removes an individual item from the queue; the file itself remains on the disk.
tour.main.queue.summary: The summary is specific to one selected run: shows its status, current photo, and how many items are ready, waiting, or failed. After processing is completed, the result remains here.
To view another queue, click on its name in the list. The consumption of the selected run and the total consumption of the history are shown separately.
tour.main.queue.parameters: These are the selected task’s saved settings: its service, model and other processing parameters. Use the separate button to apply the available concurrency limit. Local mode processes one photo at a time.
tasks are opened with a separate command. Changing them does not mean that the already created queue received a different model or a different composition of results.
tour.main.queue.history: History helps you return to information about previous tasks: when they were completed, how they ended, and what costs are known. If you have a large number of records, use pages and available filters.
History and work queue list solve different problems. Clearing scheduled work does not delete expense history or saved descriptions.
tour.main.library.overview: The library stores search information: photo paths, descriptions, and tags. Here you can check connected folders, deal with inaccessible files and exact copies, transfer program data, or clear the thumbnail cache.
button in the header only rereads the library summary. File scanning and new recognition are launched separately. The original photos themselves remain in their folders on the disk.
tour.main.library.roots: This list helps you see the folders the library works with, check their availability, and update information. This is useful when photos are located on multiple drives or in different locations.

If the folder has been moved or the drive is offline, check the path. Removing a connection to a library and deleting files on disk are different actions; refer to the description of the selected command.
tour.main.library.maintenance: Here you can find entries that have problems with the path or availability of the file. Checking helps you figure out which photos have been moved, which are no longer available, and where you need to update your information.
Check the entry’s status and path before choosing an action. Removing a library entry does not restore a missing original file.
tour.main.library.duplicates: collects verified identical files into groups. Open the group and compare the paths: the checkmarks indicate which copies you want to keep.
keeps the files and removes their group from the results, remembering your decision. It works the same in a group card and in comparison. Use
to include those groups again. Before choosing Keep marked, check the selection carefully: unmarked copies are deleted. Keep at least one copy.
tour.main.library.backup: saves descriptions, tags, collections, history and projects of the editor with its images and masks. External original photographs and API keys are not included in this copy - they must be transferred separately.

first shows details of the selected copy. After preparing the import and the next launch, the data will be restored according to the composition shown; this is replacing the relevant data, not adding photos to the folder. Deferred imports can be canceled before they are applied. Paid tasks from the copy are not automatically launched.
tour.main.library.cache: The cache stores prepared thumbnails so that the list of photos opens faster. These are supporting images for display purposes and not your originals.
Clearing the cache frees the space it occupies. The app rebuilds thumbnails when you browse again, so some previews may take longer to appear.
tour.main.library.technical: The version of the library database and the path to its file are shown here. This information helps you check what data the program is working with and troubleshoot problems.
This is the program data location, not the original photo folder. For normal work, you do not need to manually modify the database file.
tour.main.journal.overview: The log shows the history of actions with photos and program data. It helps you understand when the information changed and which file the action belonged to.
Select the desired log area and open the entry details if you want to review the changes. Technical logs of the application are located separately - click on the “Logs” button in the top line.
tour.editor.overview: The editor works with the image itself. At the top are markup tools and saving commands, on the left are operations, in the center is a photograph, and on the right are editing conditions and tasks. The frame history is stored below.
creates a final file or replaces the source with the selected result. Let's look at these actions separately.
tour.editor.top.back: Saves the project and returns to the photos or view from which the editor was opened. If you need to choose what to do with unsaved changes when exiting, the program will show you the options.
Closing a window should not be confused with canceling an already running cloud edit. Its state and the results obtained are stored in editor tasks while the program continues to run.
tour.editor.top.operations-panel: The left panel contains cropping, resizing and AI edits. Choose the operation you want here.
In a narrow window, use the top button to open this panel. Point, region and mask tools in the top row specify where to edit; they do not choose the operation.
tour.editor.top.restart: Starts a new project from the original image. This is convenient if you want to try a different edit path without continuing the current chain of changes.
The previous project is kept separately. Starting over differs from undoing the last brush stroke or selecting an earlier image in the history.
tour.editor.tools.overview: The tools at the top let you select markup, move the image and indicate where to edit. A

Choose the best way to specify the location: a reference point, a rectangle or a painted shape. Support for markup, and how closely it is followed, depend on the operation and model. Check the resulting photo after editing.
tour.editor.tools.select: Select an existing annotation to work on it. This is useful when a photo has several points, areas or masks and you want to refine the instructions for one of them.
The annotation list on the right shows which annotation is selected, whether it is visible and whether it is included in the request.
tour.editor.tools.pan: Allows you to move the enlarged photo in the viewing area. Select the tool, hold down the left mouse button on the canvas and drag the image.
This changes the viewing position. The contents of the photo and the position of objects within the photo itself do not change.
tour.editor.tools.point: Place a point to indicate where you want the edit, then enter instructions for that annotation. For example, use a point to show where a small new object should appear.
The dot represents a location, not an exact shape. If you need to outline a complex area, use a mask supported by the selected model.
tour.editor.tools.region: Draw a rectangle around the area to which the task relates. An area is useful when you want to specify part of a scene along with a small surrounding area.
The instructions explain what should change inside the area. Support for areas, and how closely their boundaries are followed, depend on the model.
tour.editor.top.more-tools: Point, region and mask tools specify where to edit. Rotation and flip controls are nearby. In a wide window these buttons appear directly on the top toolbar.
In a narrow window, some tools move to the three-dot menu. This tutorial shows their location without applying changes.
tour.editor.top.orientation: Rotation changes the orientation of the frame by a quarter turn, and mirroring flips it in the selected direction. These commands help prepare the frame before further editing.
Check the resulting image and markup. During some operations, transformations are temporarily unavailable so as not to change the basis of the work being performed.
tour.editor.tools.brush: The brush diameter sets stroke width in source-image pixels. Use a larger brush for broad areas and a smaller one near edges.
This field applies to the mask brush and eraser. With another tool selected, the tutorial shows the field disabled and keeps your current tool.
tour.editor.top.compare: to select two images in the history at the bottom, then open comparison. This helps you see what changed and which result works better.
For comparison, two frames of the current work are needed. It does not send images to the model and does not create a new result.
tour.editor.top.zoom: These controls zoom the photo out or in.
shows the image at actual size; Fit makes the whole image visible again.
The viewing scale does not change the number of pixels in the file. For this purpose, use the “Resize” operation on the left.
tour.editor.top.project-save: Saves the working image, settings, annotations and history so you can continue editing later. You can also save with
This is saving the program project. The external photo file from this command is not replaced - there is a “Save image” for it.
tour.editor.top.image-save: Saves the displayed frame to a file. You can choose to make a separate copy or replace the original image, if that option is available.
Before replacing, check the selected frame. Saving a copy is convenient when you want to keep the original file and use the result separately.
tour.editor.top.parameters: Shows or hides the right panel containing edit settings, tasks and sources. Hiding it gives the photo more room in a small window.
Hiding the panel does not mean canceling the job. The status of a running edit can be viewed by opening the “Tasks” tab.
tour.editor.top.menu: Project management, change history, project transfer and autosave settings are collected here. Exporting the project is needed to transfer the editor's work; saving an image - to obtain a regular file with the result.
If autosave is off, save the project with the save button or
. Applying a crop or mask and starting an edit saves the data needed for that operation. Save any later local changes manually.
tour.editor.top.help: The ? button opens the editor’s tour and reference. The tour follows this window’s tools, operations, canvas, edit settings, tasks and history.
A slide-out switch nearby controls tooltips throughout the program. It does not disable the ability to reopen explicit help.
tour.editor.operations.overview: with the photo. At the top are local operations - cropping and resizing. Below are neural network edits: their result depends on the selected model and task.
The point, region, and mask specify the location, and the operation defines the action. For example, the same mask can indicate an area for object deletion or other supported edits.
tour.editor.operations.crop: Cropping leaves the selected portion of the photo and removes the edges outside the frame. Move the frame, change it using the handles, or set dimensions in the fields. Aspect ratio presets, such as 16:9, help prepare the frame with the desired shape.
The frame is only a preview until you apply it. Apply the crop to create the cropped image, or cancel it to return to the previous view. Switching operations does not apply an unfinished crop.
tour.editor.operations.resize: Sets the width and height of the image in pixels. With the
setting, the width and height change consistently to maintain the shape of the photo.
The operation resizes the frame locally. If you want the model to add detail when zooming in, there is another command - “Increase detail”.
tour.editor.operations.universal: Use this for changes best described in words, such as the atmosphere of a scene or the appearance of part of the photo. Describe the desired result, then choose a model and its settings.
Markings and additional pictures help clarify the task if the model supports them. Available options are shown based on the selected model.
tour.editor.operations.replace: Use this operation to add an object to the scene or replace an existing one. Describe the object itself and the desired change; if necessary, indicate the location with a dot, area, or mask.
For example: “Add a small red ball to the empty part of the table.” If you attach an additional picture, explain which elements to use from it.
tour.editor.operations.remove: Helps remove unnecessary objects and fill free space. For a model with a mask, paint over the object to be removed, carefully refine the boundaries and apply the mask.
Some models need text, others just need a mask. The task field and the explanation next to it show what is used in the current version.
tour.editor.operations.remove-background: Separates the object you want to keep from its background. If the model accepts text, specify which object to keep. For automatic background removal, choose the appropriate model and settings.
If you need a transparent background in the saved file, choose a format that supports transparency. The quality of complex boundaries depends on the model and the original image.
tour.editor.operations.replace-backgroun: Describe the environment you want to replace the previous background: for example, “a bright studio with soft daylight.” The task relates to the new background, and not to the description of the entire previous photograph.
After receiving the result, check the main object and its boundaries. The model can change small details when connecting an object to a new environment.
tour.editor.operations.outpaint: Adds space beyond the edges of the photo to allow the model to continue the scene. The size of the future canvas can be set by the margins or frame on the image.
This is the addition of new areas, rather than stretching the original image. Detailed dimensions and optional auto-crop of the result are on the right.
tour.editor.operations.upscale: Uses the model to increase resolution and restore visible detail. The ratio and available settings depend on the option selected.
Consider the result in magnification: the model can add details that are not visible in the source image. To simply change the number of pixels without such additional drawing, use “Resize”.
tour.editor.operations.relight: Allows you to describe other light, shadows, or the atmosphere of a scene. For example: “Warm evening light on the right, soft shadows.”
To edit a specific section, use the markings supported by the model. Then check how the new lighting matches the rest of the photo.
tour.editor.operations.recolor: Helps change the color of an object or the overall color scheme. Name the object and desired color; To change a separate section, check the location using the available markings.
For example: “Make the jacket dark green, keep its folds and lighting.” So the task indicates both the desired color and the properties that are important to preserve.
tour.editor.operations.compose: Combines the original image and additional images according to your description. Explain what to take from each image and how to arrange the elements in the overall scene.
The model determines how many input images it accepts and how they can be used. Before starting, check the attachments and cost estimate on the right.
tour.editor.operations.restore: Suitable for old or damaged photographs: the model can reduce defects and improve the visibility of details. Available recovery methods depend on the selected model.
Compare the result with the original, especially faces and small objects. The model can approximately recreate completely lost details.
tour.editor.canvas.overview: The canvas shows the working image, markings and preliminary frames. The scale helps you see details, and the tools in the top panel help you indicate the area of ​​change.

Before you start editing, check the image here and the assignments on the right. The selected annotation helps edit its conditions; The visibility of a label itself does not determine whether it is included in the request.
tour.editor.canvas.outpaint-frame: Drag a corner or side of the frame to change the future borders of the image. Hold the left button inside the frame to move it relative to the original photo.

This way you can add more space on the desired side while maintaining a clear size of the canvas. If the frame cuts off part of the source, you will first need to apply pre-cropping - this action is shown in the options on the right.
tour.editor.inspector.overview: tab contains markup, job, model and run.
shows the submitted edits and their results.
helps you add images used in your project.
These are parts of the same work: first prepare the task, then run the appropriate model and evaluate the resulting frames in the tasks and the bottom history.
tour.editor.markup.overview: This list contains the current image’s points, areas and masks. Select an annotation to check whether it is included in the request and see its additional images.
An annotation has two independent settings:
. Hiding it on the image does not necessarily exclude it from the task.
tour.editor.markup.controls: The eye shows or hides the annotation on the image. The checkbox controls whether it is included in the request. The trash button removes it from the current annotations.
Before starting, check the enable flags. Selecting one line for editing does not disable other enabled jobs.
tour.editor.markup.mask-apply: While you are drawing, the mask consists of prepared strokes.
collects them into a mask for further work, and
After applying the mask, check its shape and whether it is included in the request. The eraser refines the painted area without erasing the photo.
tour.editor.instruction.overview: Here you set the result you want to get from the model. The name of the field changes along with the operation: for example, what to add, what background to make, or how to change the light.
Describe the change you want and the important properties that should be preserved. This text is a task for editing, and not a caption or description of a photograph for the library.
tour.editor.instruction.target: selects which instructions you are editing: the whole image, a point or an area. Switch between entries to prepare several locations in turn.
A run includes all enabled annotations with non-empty instructions for the current operation, not just the selected row. The whole-image instructions are included as well.
