tour.editor.instruction.text: Name the action, object, and important properties of the result. For example:

children: "Add a small red ball to the table, keep the lighting and other items"

tour.editor.instruction.text: Use annotations to specify a particular part of the image. If the chosen model only needs a mask or settings and does not accept text, an explanation appears instead of the input field.
tour.editor.references.whole: These pictures support the general instructions for the entire photo. Add a file with the plus button or drag an image from the bottom filmstrip, then explain in the instructions what to use from it.

Selecting an individual annotation hides this shared section, but keeps its attachments. They can still be included in the request. The model’s overall image limit includes the original and any additional pictures used.
tour.editor.references.mark: Pictures attached to a point or area belong to that annotation’s instructions. They help show which object or appearance you want at that location.
A point accepts one additional image; adding another replaces it. An area can accept several images within the model’s total limit. Masks do not have this attachment block.
tour.editor.references.limits: Before starting, check which pictures are included and which tasks they relate to. The number of available inputs is limited to the selected model and includes the original image.
When the limit is reached, adding more images is unavailable. Remove an attachment you do not need, or choose a compatible model with enough image inputs. Then check the request contents again.
tour.editor.model.overview: The model determines which edits are possible: the instructions it understands, whether it accepts masks and additional images, and the sizes and settings available. A cost estimate appears below the selected option.
Choose a suitable model, then check its settings and input images. The estimate helps you plan spending. Confirmed charges appear separately in the task.
tour.editor.model.profiles: These levels help you quickly select an option for your current operation: one that is more economical, balanced, or quality-oriented. Once selected, check the specific model in the list below.

When changing the level, the corresponding model variant is selected. Compare its capabilities and cost estimate: the names of the levels help with the choice, and specific conditions are shown for the selected model.
tour.editor.model.filters: Filters narrow the list by tier, estimated cost for the run, resolution and number of additional pictures, excluding the original. You can also find models that let you request the original photo dimensions.
If nothing is found, loosen the conditions or reset the filters. A size match means you can request it; The selected model performs internal image processing according to its own rules.
tour.editor.model.details: Open the model details to check support for annotations and additional pictures, available dimensions and the selected option’s features. Models may interpret the same mask or instructions differently.
The rate and cost estimate help you plan spending. If billing depends on tokens or processing time, the estimate can differ from the service’s actual charge.
tour.editor.model.output: Here you set the result parameters available to the model: for example, size, quality or number of images. The composition of the fields depends on the selected option.
Before starting, check the parameters and cost estimate together. The size you enter is the requested size; the task shows the actual dimensions of the returned file.
tour.editor.outpaint.size: fields specify the added space in pixels. Below you can specify the

If the planned frame cuts into the original photo, apply the preliminary crop with the available button first. Then start generating the additional space. Use the frame on the canvas together with the size fields to position it precisely.
tour.editor.model.advanced: This block contains the remaining parameters of the selected model. Fields with their own explanations help you understand what the setting affects and what values ​​are allowed.

The JSON mode is intended for accurately specifying additional model fields. For general editing, start with the basic settings; The technical names of the parameters in JSON must correspond to the selected model.
tour.editor.model.limits: The per-run budget is checked against the estimate before sending. An edit estimated above that limit will not start. An enabled period budget covers several runs. Actual service charges are shown separately.
limits how many requests run in parallel. It helps control load and spending; it does not shorten each individual request.
tour.editor.model.inputs: Check the prepared request here: images, masks and parameters that will be sent. This is especially useful when a project has many annotations and additional pictures.
Cloud editing requires an API key for the chosen service. Add it with the separate button. Opening the request details does not start generation.
tour.editor.launch: Before starting, check the working image, enabled annotations, instructions, model and estimated cost. The button submits the prepared edit. If needed, the app first asks you to confirm sending the images.
While the current edit is in progress, restarting is not available. If it fails or is interrupted, open Tasks: it shows the status and available actions for the previous request.
tour.editor.jobs.overview: Edits you have submitted are listed here. Expand a card to see its model, timing, dimensions, results and costs.

selects an image already received without generating it again. Confirmed charges and unconfirmed estimates appear separately, so you can distinguish known costs from amounts still awaiting confirmation.
tour.editor.jobs.recovery: If execution is interrupted after sending, an available continuation command helps retrieve and save the result of the previous request. There is no need to create a new edit just because the result has not finished loading.

If the program does not know whether the submission was accepted, use the suggested reconciliation of the previous request. It is different from the new generation. The status “Queued by the service” means waiting on the service side, not a ready result.
tour.editor.jobs.cancel: The cancel cross applies to this running task. It does not affect all projects or delete a photo. After cancelling, check the card’s updated status.
If the service has already accepted the request, cancellation does not automatically result in a refund. The resulting status and known consumption are stored in the task details.
tour.editor.sources.overview: Here are the images available to the project. They can be added from a file, selected from an archive, or downloaded via a direct HTTPS link to the image.

Click an image to use it as the working image. The separate add button attaches it as an additional source for the current edit. This lets you use another photo as material without changing the working image.
tour.editor.sources.roles: In additional sources, select the role of the image:
. This role explains how to use the material; arrows change the order of sources in the query.
A cross excludes the picture from additional sources. The image itself remains among the project materials and can be used again.
tour.editor.history.overview: The bottom strip contains the images you worked with and the results you received. Select an image to view it and continue working from it.
History lets you compare versions without looking for files in folders. You can also drag an image into a supported additional-pictures section to use it in another edit.
tour.editor.history.compare: and select two frames of history, then click the compare button in the top bar. This way you can compare the source and the result, or two different options.
The comparison shows existing frames. It does not create a new request and does not replace the file on disk with the selected option.
tour.editor.history.branches: Open the tree to see which frame each version came from. Levels run from left to right, and a frame can have several branches.

Use the wheel to zoom and the middle button to pan the map. Click to select a frame; double-click or press Enter to preview it. “Use this frame” makes it the working frame. Move or resize the preview window; inside it, use the wheel to zoom the photo and the middle button to pan. Ctrl-click two frames to compare them.
tour.viewer.overview: The viewer helps you look at the photo, zoom in on details, and move on to adjacent photos. The main actions are at the top, zoom and display controls are at the bottom.
You can hide panels for quiet viewing or run a slide show. These modes are different from normal photo enlargement; Let's look at them after the main buttons.
tour.viewer.top.overview: At the top are the transition to the editor, rotation, deletion, printing and sending of the photo. Additional commands are grouped into a three-dot menu, with help and window controls on the right.
All actions refer to the image shown. Before saving or deleting, check its name and image, especially after swiping.
tour.viewer.top.edit: Opens this photo in the Smart Photo editor. There you can crop the image, resize it, or prepare an edit using the model.
Viewing and zooming do not edit the file. Use this command to change the image. The editor has its own tour, available through Help inside its window.
tour.viewer.top.rotate: Rotates the image in view a quarter turn to the left or right. This is convenient if the photo is displayed sideways.
Rotation only changes the display in the viewer. To write the desired orientation to a file, open the editor, rotate the image in it and save the image.
tour.viewer.top.delete: This is a command to delete a photo, not to close the viewing window. Before using it, check the name and the image shown, especially if you quickly flipped through the files.
To simply end browsing, use the close window button on the right.
tour.viewer.top.print: Opens printing for the current photo. In the print dialog, choose an available printer and check the settings before sending the job.
Enlarging the image in the viewer helps you see the details, but print settings are selected separately.
tour.viewer.top.share: Opens an accessible way to transfer the current photo through Windows tools. Applications and options vary by system.
This command applies to a photo file. To transfer descriptions and tags between libraries, there is XMP and data export in the main window.
tour.viewer.top.more: The menu contains additional actions with the current photo and setting up a future opening without panels. The availability of individual commands depends on the file and the capabilities of Windows.
Select the desired action from within the menu. Expanding the list itself does not save the image or launch the editor.
tour.viewer.menu.resize: Opens preparation for photo resizing. Check the width, height and save option before applying.
This is a change to a file or a saved copy of it. This is different from the viewing scale in the bottom panel, which helps you view the photo without changing the number of pixels.
tour.viewer.menu.file-actions: creates a copy of the original file: the scale and rotation of the view are not recorded in it. To save the changed frame, use the editor using the top button
Through the same menu you can show the file in its folder or open an external editor assigned to Windows. It may differ from the editor Smart Photo.
tour.viewer.top.help: The question mark opens the viewer’s Help. Explore this window’s controls in order, or find a topic in Reference.
A slide-out switch nearby turns hover annotations on and off. Explicit help with "?" available regardless of it.
tour.viewer.top.window: These buttons minimize the window, change its size, or close the view. A maximized window gives more space to the photo while maintaining control of the viewer.
Window size, Photo Only mode, and Slideshow are different viewing methods. The slide show additionally scrolls through photos by time.
tour.viewer.image.overview: The current photo is shown here. Zoom in on the part you want, then pan the image to see details outside the visible area.
Zooming and moving only changes the view. If the image could not be opened, a message appears on the canvas indicating the reason; check it before further actions with the file.
tour.viewer.image.neighbors: Arrows along the edges move to the previous or next photo of the open set. If a file is opened separately from Windows, available adjacent photos are taken from its folder.
With one image available, there is nothing to swipe through, so the arrows may not appear. Normal zooming and panning of a photo works regardless of the number of neighbors.
tour.viewer.image.panels: In normal view, double-clicking a photo hides the top and bottom panels; double-clicking again brings them back. More space is freed up for the image.
The action is also available for an enlarged, shifted image. In a slideshow, double-clicking does another thing: it ends the show.
tour.viewer.bottom.overview: On the left are favorites and file information, in the middle are the interval and display start, and on the right are zoom controls.
These commands help you evaluate the quality of the image and choose a convenient viewing method. Let's start with information, then we'll look at display and magnification.
tour.viewer.bottom.favorite: The star adds the photo to favorites or unstars it. This way you can mark successful pictures right while viewing.
In the main window they will be available in the
tab. Marking does not create a copy of the file or change its image.
tour.viewer.bottom.details: Opens information about the current file. They help check the name, location and known parameters of the image.
The resolution and file size are also visible in the bottom line when data is available. An unknown value means no information read, not a photo size of zero.
tour.viewer.bottom.interval: Here you select how long one photo is displayed before moving on to the next. A short interval is convenient for quick viewing, a long interval gives time to look at the photo.
Selecting an interval by itself does not trigger the display. To start, click the adjacent slide show button.
tour.viewer.bottom.actual-size: to view the photo without shrinking it to fit into the window. A large picture may not fit entirely.
Drag the enlarged image to inspect different areas. Use Fit to see the whole photo again.
tour.viewer.bottom.zoom: The list, slider and buttons change the scale of the current photo. The percentage shows how much it is increased or decreased relative to the actual size.
This helps to see the details, but does not add them to the file. To change the image resolution, use a separate resizing command or editor.
tour.viewer.bottom.fit: Selects a scale at which it is convenient to see the entire photo in an accessible area. It's a quick way to get back from looking at small details to getting the big picture.
Fit is different from maximizing a window and from a slideshow: it controls the scale of the photo within the current view.
tour.viewer.slideshow.controls: During a slideshow, you can pause, move between photos or leave the show.
pauses and resumes automatic playback. Double-click or press
Controls become clearer when you hover over them. Opening Help pauses the current image. When you close Help, a previously running slideshow resumes; a pause you set yourself stays in place.
tour.main.settings.overview: Five tabs group the settings: general, recognition, queue, storage and projects. Choose a tab in the top row.
Changes apply through each field. There is no global Save button. Switching tabs does not start processing or install a model.
tour.main.settings.general: Choose the language, theme, hover hints and photo-only viewer here. Below are subfolder browsing and the image filter.
Subfolder browsing here applies to the explorer. Including subfolders in recognition is a separate option on the Recognition tab.
tour.main.settings.recognition: Choose local processing or an available cloud service, then a model. Local models have installation and checking controls; cloud services have fields to enter and check your own key.
Below are processing subfolders, smart names, copies, skipping existing results and cloud consent. Changing the service does not send photos. Unavailable choices remain disabled.
tour.main.settings.queue: Set request delay, retries, passes, parallel cloud requests, response limits and image size here. These values control photo recognition.
Queue behavior after restart is configured separately below. Check the limits before a large new batch; changing tabs does not start waiting jobs.
tour.main.settings.storage: Recognition copies and editor image exports have separate destinations. For each group, choose beside the source, a separate folder or another available option.
The editor’s internal storage and cache are shown below. These differ from the folder for exported photos. Cancelling folder selection keeps the previous destination.
tour.main.settings.projects: Autosave saves a changed project at the selected interval. “Always save on close” is a separate setting. Both settings are shared with the editor.
A project stores frames and history; the photo file is saved separately. The management button opens shared project storage, where you can review the list and size before cleanup.
tour.main.library.projects: This section shows the number of editor projects and their disk usage. Open management to prepare cleanup for selected photos, all projects or projects before a date.

The app first lists the exact projects and estimated space. Deletion needs separate confirmation; open projects and unfinished jobs are protected. Source and exported photos remain, but cleaned project history becomes unavailable.
tour.editor.project.preferences: Autosave saves a changed project at the selected interval. “Always save on close” is a separate setting. Both settings are shared with the editor.
A project stores frames and history; the photo file is saved separately. The management button opens shared project storage, where you can review the list and size before cleanup.
